title: Assistant Vice President, Planning & Environmental
description:
Want to be a part of something bigger than yourself? To contribute to a team making moves on a global scale? Then you’re invited to join the team that lives the So Cal, So Easy vibe. The phenomenal team works daily to connect people, places and create experiences for the millions of passengers traveling through Southern California’s Ontario International Airport (ONT). ONT is looking for people who think outside of the box, who get excited about the possibilities, and who want to continue paving the way for the fastest growing airport in the U.S. If you want to be a part of a vibrant team making world-class moves, and contribute to shaping the future of this airport, region and industry, then look no further. #ThisisONT.

The future of ONT starts now. Through the ONT BOLD (Building Our Legacy & Destiny) Program, you can be a part of one of Southern California’s most ambitious airport development programs. ONT BOLD is transforming Ontario International Airport with a new terminal, modernized facilities, and infrastructure improvements designed to support future growth—and we’re looking for visionary leaders to help make it happen.

COMPENSATION

$185,000 - $215,000 annual salary + a generous benefits package to include medical, dental, vision and 10% employer paid 401A through VOYA Financial.

*Hiring Salary Range: $185,000 - $200,000 annual salary

(starting salary will be within this range based upon qualifications)


SUMMARY

The Assistant Vice President, Planning and Environmental (AVP, P&E) is a senior leader at the Ontario International Airport Authority (OIAA), reporting to the Vice President of Capital Development. The AVP, P&E provides strategic oversight for OIAA’s long-range planning and environmental functions, driving long-term development strategies, capital investment programs, and regulatory compliance to help shape the framework for ONT’s continued growth and transformation.

This role leads the planning and environmental framework supporting ONT’s growth, overseeing airport planning, environmental planning, a006Ed sustainability activities that support OIAA’s capital program and major infrastructure initiatives. The position leads the planning and development activities associated with the Capital Improvement Program (CIP) and ensures alignment between development plans and operational priorities, and long-range development initiative BOLD (Building Our Legacy and Destiny)

Collaborating with the Vice President and OIAA divisions, the AVP, P&E translates strategic objectives and stakeholder needs into actionable development plans. As a senior advisor, the position addresses airport development, regulatory requirements, and land use. The position provides executive-level direction on complex and often interdependent development issues, identifies opportunities and risks, and advances solutions that support ONT’s evolving role as a major regional transportation asset.

The AVP, P&E also sets planning priorities, manages consultants, and builds relationships with airlines, tenants, regulatory agencies, and community stakeholders, ensuring that ONT’s future development is strategic, environmentally responsible, and aligned with OIAA’s long-term vision.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Important and essential duties may include, but are not limited to, the following:

· Strategic Leadership:
Provide comprehensive oversight for the airport's planning and environmental functions, ensuring alignment with OIAA’s long-term goals and operational requirements. Establish and communicate the strategic vision for planning and environmental initiatives. Ensure airport development strategies and capital planning efforts are informed by sound planning principles, environmental stewardship, regulatory requirements, operational considerations, and long-term financial objectives.

· Collaborative Development:
Partner with the Vice President and cross-functional teams to translate strategic objectives into actionable development strategies. Lead discussions with stakeholders to gather insights and adapt strategies to meet evolving needs.

· Planning Oversight:
Lead and direct the development, implementation and execution of airport planning initiatives, including long-range development plans, facility studies, and aviation planning efforts, including the BOLD Program. Regularly assess and update plans to reflect changing operational landscapes.

· Environmental Planning:
Oversee environmental planning and compliance activities associated with airport development, ensuring adherence to all relevant federal, state, and local regulations. Coordinate environmental studies, permitting, and agency approvals to facilitate development projects.

· Stakeholder Engagement:
Coordinates closely with other OIAA Divisions and Departments, including Finance, Operations, Revenue Management, Airline Affairs, Administration, Procurement, and other OIAA functions to ensure effective integration of planning and environmental requirements into capital projects. Foster strong relationships with airlines, tenants, regulatory agencies, governmental entities, and community stakeholders. Represent OIAA in public forums and cultivate partnerships that support airport development initiatives.

· Project Coordination:
Manage the integration of planning activities with the Capital Improvement Program (CIP), ensuring consistency with long-term development plans and organizational priorities. Coordinate multidisciplinary teams to advance capital projects effectively.

· Risk Management:
Identify potential planning, environmental, regulatory, operational, and stakeholder risks associated with development initiatives. Develop and implement strategies to mitigate these risks and ensure project success.

· Sustainability Leadership:
Lead initiatives related to sustainability, climate resilience, and environmental stewardship. Advocate for practices that support OIAA’s long-term environmental and operational objectives.

· Metrics and Analysis:
Develop and maintain planning metrics, forecasts, and risk assessments. Utilize analytical tools to support informed decision-making regarding capital investments and development strategies. Provides technical and strategic input into capital project prioritization, project programming, scope development, cost considerations, phasing, implementation strategies, and development sequencing

PROFILE OF THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

· Proven Leadership Experience:
Significant senior leadership experience in managing complex airport planning, environmental, or infrastructure programs within aviation, transportation, or similarly complex and highly regulated environments. A track record of developing and executing long-range strategies that drive organizational growth.

· Expertise in Airport Planning:
Demonstrated ability to develop and execute long-range airport planning and development strategies that support organizational growth, operational requirements, financial objectives, and stakeholder expectations. Deep understanding of airport planning principles, including master planning, aviation demand forecasting, environmental review, and capital program integration. Familiarity with FAA regulations and industry best practices.

· Complex Environmental Planning:
Demonstrated experience leading intricate environmental planning and regulatory compliance activities associated with major infrastructure or airport development projects. Knowledge of environmental laws and sustainability practices.

· Analytical and Strategic Decision-Making:
Highly skilled in analytical decision-making, project prioritization, and multidisciplinary problem-solving. Ability to translate complex technical issues into actionable recommendations for executive leadership and stakeholders.

· Stakeholder Management:
Strong ability to build collaborative relationships with FAA and other regulatory agencies, airlines, local governments, and community stakeholders. Proven experience in managing diverse expectations and fostering consensus.

· Project Management:
Experience managing multiple high-priority initiatives in dynamic environments while maintaining strategic focus and accountability. Ability to oversee consultancy teams and ensure quality deliverables.

· Communication and Presentation Skills:
Exceptional communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to present complex planning and environmental matters to executive and public audiences effectively. Strong negotiation skills and emotional intelligence to navigate diverse stakeholder interests.

· Commitment to Sustainability:
A strong advocate for sustainable airport development and innovation, with a demonstrated commitment to continuous improvement and operational excellence.

· Educational Background:
A Bachelor’s degree in Airport or Urban Planning, Environmental Science, Aviation Management, Civil Engineering or a related field is required, with a Master’s degree and professional certifications preferred.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Any combination of education, training, and experience that would likely provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities is qualifying.

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Airport Planning, Urban Planning, City and Regional Planning, Environmental Planning, Environmental Science, Civil Engineering, Airport Planning, Aviation Management, Architecture, Public Administration, or a related field is required.
  • Minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in airport planning, aviation planning, environmental planning, infrastructure development, transportation planning, land use planning, or a closely related field.
  • Minimum of three (3) years of progressively responsible management or leadership experience overseeing multidisciplinary planning, environmental, infrastructure, or development functions.
  • Demonstrated experience leading complex airport planning, master planning, environmental review, infrastructure planning, or major development initiatives is required.
  • Experience working with the FAA and other federal, state, and local regulatory or governmental agencies on airport development, planning, environmental, or infrastructure matters is highly desirable.
  • Experience working within or alongside a public agency, airport authority, transportation agency, or similarly complex and highly regulated organization is highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated experience managing planning and environmental consultants, technical studies, regulatory processes, and multidisciplinary project teams is preferred.
  • Master’s degree in Urban Planning, City and Regional Planning, Environmental Planning, Environmental Science, Engineering, Public Administration, Aviation Management, or a related field is preferred.
  • Professional credentials such as American Institute of Certified Planners (AICP), Professional Engineer (PE), Certified Environmental Professional, or other relevant professional certification are highly desirable.

LICENSES / CERTIFICATION

  • Valid Driver’s License equivalent to a California Class C Driver’s license
  • Acceptable driving record at time of appointment and throughout employment
  • Ability to pass all background / reference checks, knowledge examinations, as well as aptitude tests necessary to obtain an OIAA employee badge at ONT

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Finger dexterity to utilize a keyboard to input information on a computer
  • Ability to lift and carry files and other media weighing up to twenty-five (25) pounds up to a distance of approximately 20 feet
  • Ability to open filing cabinets and bend or stand as necessary
  • Ability to access areas owned or leased by OIAA

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee might encounter while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Climate controlled office environment
  • Passenger airline terminals including operations areas not open to the public
  • Construction job sites where extreme conditions may exist
  • Non climate-controlled areas where there may be exposure to fumes or airborne particles, moving mechanical parts, and vibration

This is an at-will, exempt position. Only a valid and properly executed employment agreement may alter status as an at-will employee. Verbal contracts are not valid. The employment relationship may be terminated at the will of either party upon notice to the other. As an at-will employee, there would not be an established property interest in continued employment with OIAA.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

  • Candidates who successfully complete all phases of the selection process will be placed on an eligibility list. Current and future vacancies will be filled from this list. Lists typically last for 6 months but may be extended or abolished based upon the needs of the Ontario International Airport Authority (OIAA).
  • The OIAA encourages applications from qualified individuals with disabilities as defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act and the Fair Employment and Housing Act. Individuals who require a reasonable accommodation to participate in any phase of the selection process must make such a request during the application process. Applicants with disabilities that affect sensory, manual, or speaking skills may be provided with a test in a format that does not require the use of the impaired skill. Persons requesting reasonable accommodation will be required to provide documentation of such a need.
  • The OIAA supports a Drug-Free Workplace. The pre-employment physical may include a drug screen where permitted by law.
  • Successful candidates shall be required to complete a verification form designated by the Department of Homeland Security United States Citizenship and Immigration Services that certifies eligibility for employment in the United States of America.
  • All potential employees are required to pass a fingerprint review and may be required to pass a pre-employment physical examination prior to appointment.
  • Employees are required to successfully complete all background / reference checks, knowledge examinations, as well as aptitude tests necessary to obtain an OIAA employee badge at ONT.
  • The provisions of this bulletin do not constitute a contract expressed or implied and any provisions contained in this posting may be modified or revoked without notice.
  • If applicable, official college transcripts may be required prior to receiving an offer of employment.

title: Senior Bioinformatics Research Scientist
description:
The Senior Bioinformatics Research Scientist performs data analysis, data visualization, statistical analysis, experimental design, database development, mathematical modeling, and novel method development. Provides bioinformatics analysis for investigators and communicates analytical process and results.

St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital’s Pediatric Translational Neuroscience Initiative (PTNI) is dedicated to understanding and treating catastrophic childhood neurological diseases. PTNI bridges basic and clinical neuroscience, partnering with industry and foundations to accelerate the translation of novel therapies from bench to bedside. The Center for Pediatric Neurological Disease Research (CPNDR), PTNI’s basic science arm, houses the McKinnon Lab, which is seeking a Senior Bioinformatics Research Scientist to lead sequencing and multi-omics analysis pipelines.

We’re looking for a self-starter with deep expertise in bioinformatics and human genetics, a genuine commitment to neurological disease research, and exceptional communication skills. The ideal candidate stays at the forefront of emerging tools and technologies and uses that knowledge to expand CPNDR’s analytical capabilities.


This scientist will independently design and implement analytical strategies across multiple genomics platforms, interpret complex datasets, and translate findings for diverse audiences. These include principal investigators, laboratory personnel with limited computational backgrounds, collaborating laboratories, and institutional core facilities. The role requires strong project ownership and the ability to prioritize competing demands across laboratory research initiatives as scientific needs evolve.


The successful candidate will apply advanced problem-solving and independent scientific judgment, not simply execute established workflows under supervision. Responsibilities include diagnosing sequencing and data-quality issues, identifying root causes of unexpected results, and developing and implementing corrective analytical strategies with minimal direction. This level of autonomy is essential to providing reliable, innovative computational support as our research portfolio continues to expand.


Areas of Focus:

  • Bulk and single-cell transcriptomics from patient cells, organoids, and animal models, supporting rare disease gene discovery and analysis
  • Analysis of patient disease mutations and cross-disorder comparisons
  • Multiple sequencing platforms, including short- and long-read technologies
  • Integration and management of multi-omics data (DNA, RNA, methylation etc.)
  • Familiarity in building or managing GUI applications and databases for multi-omic sequencing results and clinical datasets from diverse sources.

Additional Responsibilities:

  • Train and mentor PTNI and laboratory members
  • Prepare documentation and educational materials
  • Serve as liaison among researchers, institutional computational resources, and collaborating research groups
  • Establish best practices and strengthen lab-wide bioinformatics capabilities
  • Ensure computational infrastructure supports rapidly evolving research priorities

Job Responsibilities:


  • Provide research support and deliver high-quality results by formulating an efficient analytical approach with the available data.
  • Deliver data files, and document the analytical process. May participate in manuscript preparation at project's conclusion.
  • Assist with establishing and documenting protocols or best practices for common research tasks, and in the formulation of analytical plans that use the best approach to address challenging data analysis questions.
  • Assist in the evaluation and testing of new methods and technologies.
  • Contribute ideas to automate or improve existing analysis methods. Implement the improvement or work with others to do so.
  • Participate in the department's developmental projects and interdepartmental team projects.
  • Perform other duties as assigned to meet the goals and objectives of the department and institution.
  • Maintains regular and predictable attendance.

Minimum Education and/or Training:

  • Bachelor's degree in bioinformatics, cheminformatics, statistics/computer science (with a background in biological sciences or chemistry) or related field.
  • Master's degree or PhD preferred.

Minimum Experience:


  • Minimum Requirement: Bachelor's degree with 7+ years of relevant post-degree work in bioinformatics, cheminformatics, statistics/computer science (with a background in biological sciences or chemistry).
  • Experience Exception: Master's degree with 5+ years of relevant post-degree experience (OR) PhD with 2+ years of relevant post-degree experience.
  • Significant experience in at least one programming or scripting language and at least one statistical package, with R preferred.

Compensation

In recognition of certain U.S. state and municipal pay transparency laws, St. Jude is including a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This is an estimate offered in good faith and a specific salary offer takes into account factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the salary range and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current salary range is $104,000 - $186,160 per year for the role of Senior Bioinformatics Research Scientist.

title: Director of Service & Accounts (Electrical Construction)
description:
If you need assistance with the application process, please notify IB Abel’s Human Resources Department. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.


About Us

IB Abel’s 110-year history is a testament to its adaptability, forward-thinking leadership, commitment to safety, and stellar service and project delivery process. Our core values—Responsible, Integrity, Results-Oriented, Ownership, and Professional—shape everything that we do at all levels of the company and are purposefully incorporated into all company communications, meetings, and strategic planning. Our use of the EOS model (Entrepreneurial Operating System) also provides structure and clarity among all levels of the company to maintain focus on our shared goals.


IB Abel (IBA) is committed to providing ample learning and career development opportunities to its team members via our Associate's Program in Project Management, Estimating, and Accounting and our growing Learning Management System.


The Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Director of Service & Accounts who is responsible for providing effective leadership to our electrical Service & Accounts Department through all aspects of the project life cycle from business development through project close out. This position is accountable for the safety, quality, estimation, project management, and profitability of all projects and customers managed through this department.


Key Responsibilities

  • Safety & Field Compliance: Ensures a safe and incident-free workplace; perform field audits to monitor field personnel work habits and safety performance; attends company and project safety meetings; and promotes and reinforces safe work practices and compliance with company safety expectations.
  • Leadership & Team Development: Manages and develops a team of Service & Accounts Department Project Managers/Estimators and Field Personnel; provides leadership, direction, coaching, and performance management to department personnel; and fosters accountability, teamwork, and professional development across the department.
  • Operations & Project Management: Ensures resource and work schedules are maintained in coordination with appropriate departments; ensures the Service & Accounts Department consistently implements the Company's Project Management methodology and key project milestones; monitors operational performance and identify opportunities to improve departmental processes and efficiency; and maintains appropriate coordination between field personnel, project management, estimating, and other supporting departments.
  • Performance Management & Continuous Improvement: Maintains all reporting and performance indicators for the Service & Accounts Department; monitors key performance metrics and identify trends, issues, and opportunities for improvement; and recommends and implements process improvements to enhance departmental performance, efficiency, and profitability.
  • Customer Relations & Service Excellence: Develops and maintains strong relationships with existing customers; increases customer satisfaction and deepen existing customer relationships; services clients in a timely, professional, and respectful manner while meeting or exceeding customer expectations; and maintains regular communication with customers to understand their needs and ensure effective resolution of issues.
  • Financial Management: Ensures accurate and timely revenue and cost reporting; ensures team is communicating project cost inconsistencies within the organization and report any major issues to the Vice President – Electrical Services; reviews monthly reports from team detailing projected revenues and costs at project completion; refers all potential legal or contractual problems concerning projects to senior leadership; and ensures timeliness of billing and collections for Service & Accounts Department Projects.


Who We’re Looking For

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Business, or other related field or comparable equivalent of education and work experience.
  • Minimum 5 to 8 years’ experience in management/leadership roles in electrical construction related businesses and industries.
  • Strong knowledge of the local area’s construction services industry and/or other related service-oriented organizations.
  • Exhibited knowledge of industrial electrical customer’s expectations.
  • Proficient in MS Office applications with strong skills in Excel, Word, Primavera 6 and MS Project.
  • Local to York, Pennsylvania but with regular travel to other offices, customer facilities, jobsites and yard locations for offsite meetings (flexibility to work from home when appropriate).
  • A “can-do” attitude, strong work ethic, and ability to collaborate effectively with various teams.


Why Choose IBA

  • Culture of Growth: Many of our leaders started in entry-level field roles and advanced within the company.
  • Flexibility & Autonomy: We empower our team to succeed without micromanagement.
  • Competitive Compensation & Benefits: Includes competitive salary, vehicle allowance program, 401(k) with company matching, tuition reimbursement, and comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision.
  • Stability & Variety: Work for multi-generational family-oriented business on diverse, fast-paced projects without the stress of a large corporate structure.
  • Incentives: Performance-based bonuses/incentives and a progressive PTO programs that grows with your tenure!
  • Collaboration: A team environment where we work together to solve challenges and celebrate wins.


Step Into a Career That Powers the Future!


IB Abel is an equal opportunity employer, all qualified applicants are encouraged to apply.

title: Jr. .NET Engineer
description:
Job Description:

About DXC

DXC helps global companies run their mission-critical systems and operations while modernizing IT, optimizing data architectures and ensuring security and scalability across public, private and hybrid clouds. The world's largest companies and public sector organizations trust DXC to deploy services that drive new levels of performance, competitiveness, and customer experience across their IT estates. Our more than 125,000 people in 70-plus countries are entrusted by our customers to deliver transformative technologies to ensure the success, safety, and well-being of businesses and people around the world. By combining strengths and expertise globally, we create solutions and deliver greater outcomes for customers across their entire IT estate. Learn more about how we deliver excellence for our customers and colleagues at DXC.

About the Role

We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Jr. .NET Core Engineer to join our Applications team in Guadalajara, Mexico. This role is ideal for an early-career software engineer looking to gain hands-on experience developing enterprise-scale backend services and REST APIs using modern Microsoft technologies.

The successful candidate will contribute to the development, maintenance, testing, and troubleshooting of backend applications within an Agile/Scrum environment. Working alongside developers, QA engineers, Product Owners, Scrum Masters, and DevOps teams, the engineer will learn and apply industry best practices including Clean Architecture, SOLID principles, source control, CI/CD concepts, cloud technologies, and AI-assisted software development.

Essential Job Functions

  • Participate actively in Agile/Scrum ceremonies, including daily stand-ups, sprint planning, backlog refinement sessions, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.
  • Develop, enhance, maintain, and troubleshoot backend services and REST APIs using C# and .NET technologies.
  • Deliver assigned development tasks, enhancements, and defect fixes through Jira or similar work management platforms.
  • Implement and consume RESTful APIs following established enterprise standards and best practices.
  • Build efficient data-access solutions using LINQ and object-oriented programming principles.
  • Follow Clean Architecture guidelines, ensuring clear separation of concerns between controllers, services, repositories, and business logic.
  • Apply SOLID principles and software design patterns to produce maintainable, scalable, and testable code.
  • Utilize .NET Dependency Injection and understand service lifetimes including Transient, Scoped, and Singleton.
  • Test, debug, and validate API functionality using Postman and related testing tools.
  • Analyze HTTP requests and responses using Fiddler or comparable debugging and proxy tools to investigate system issues.
  • Support caching implementations using Redis and understand basic caching strategies.
  • Execute basic relational database development and troubleshooting tasks utilizing SQL and technologies such as MySQL.
  • Work with feature flags and feature toggles to support safe delivery and controlled feature releases.
  • Utilize Git workflows including branching, commits, pull requests, merges, and conflict resolution.
  • Participate in code reviews and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Develop a foundational understanding of Docker containers and containerized application environments.
  • Collaborate with DevOps teams and understand CI/CD concepts, including GitHub Actions and deployment pipelines.
  • Support cloud-based application initiatives and environments utilizing AWS services.
  • Use AI-assisted development tools responsibly to support coding, debugging, documentation, code review, research, and routine engineering activities while validating generated outputs before implementation.
  • Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams to investigate issues, identify root causes, and deliver maintainable solutions.
  • Maintain technical documentation and follow established development standards, security practices, and quality guidelines.

Basic Qualifications

  • Knowledge of C# and .NET development.
  • Understanding of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts.
  • Basic experience developing or working with REST APIs.
  • Understanding of controllers, services, and business logic separation.
  • Familiarity with LINQ and data manipulation techniques.
  • Understanding of SOLID principles and Dependency Injection concepts.
  • Knowledge of Git and collaborative source-control workflows.
  • Knowledge of SQL and relational database fundamentals.
  • Familiarity with API testing tools such as Postman.
  • General understanding of backend application architecture.
  • Professional English communication skills for collaboration in a global environment.

Other Qualifications

AI-Assisted Development Skills

  • Familiarity with AI coding agents and AI-assisted development platforms such as OpenAI Codex, Claude, OpenCode, or comparable technologies.
  • Ability to leverage agentic workflows for code exploration, implementation support, debugging, refactoring, test generation, documentation, and research.
  • Basic prompt-engineering and context-management skills.
  • Ability to provide clear objectives, requirements, constraints, and acceptance criteria to obtain reliable AI-generated outcomes.
  • Familiarity with reusable agent instructions, standardized workflows, and development accelerators.
  • Understanding of task decomposition and the effective use of specialized AI subagents when appropriate.
  • Awareness of token efficiency, context-window management, and model-selection considerations.
  • Ability to validate, test, and review AI-generated outputs while maintaining secure coding and data-handling practices.

Preferred / Nice-to-Have Skills

  • Experience with .NET 8 or .NET 10.
  • Familiarity with Clean Architecture concepts.
  • Understanding of Redis and caching strategies.
  • Exposure to MySQL.
  • Experience with Docker fundamentals.
  • Familiarity with GitHub Actions and CI/CD concepts.
  • AWS cloud knowledge.
  • Experience using Fiddler or other HTTP debugging/proxy tools.
  • Knowledge of feature flags and feature toggle implementations.
  • Experience with Jira or similar Agile project management tools.
  • Understanding of commonly used software design patterns.
  • Hands-on experience incorporating AI-assisted development tools into software engineering workflows.

Soft Skills

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.
  • Proactive approach to learning and problem-solving.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within a team environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Willingness to ask questions and seek clarification when needed.
  • Receptiveness to feedback and continuous improvement.
  • Organization and ownership of assigned tasks and deliverables.
  • Growth mindset and eagerness to learn new technologies and practices.

Candidate Profile

This position is suitable for a graduate or junior backend developer with foundational .NET knowledge who is seeking to build experience within enterprise software development environments. The ideal candidate is eager to learn, adaptable, and passionate about software engineering best practices.

The candidate is not expected to be a DevOps engineer, cloud specialist, or AI specialist. However, they should understand the overall software-development lifecycle, including implementing and testing changes locally, managing source code, participating in CI/CD processes, supporting deployment activities, and utilizing modern AI-assisted development tools responsibly within a professional engineering workflow.

Why DXC? / Life at DXC

DXC is an employer of choice with strong values and fosters a culture of inclusion, belonging, and corporate citizenship. We inspire and take care of our people. We work to create a culture of learning, diversity, and inclusion and are dedicated to strong ethics and corporate citizenship. DXC is where talented professionals seize opportunities to advance their careers and amplify customer success. Full-time employees may be eligible to participate in DXC's comprehensive benefits programs and professional-development opportunities.

Additional Information

DXC Technology is committed to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering an inclusive workplace where all qualified applicants receive consideration for employment based on their qualifications, skills, and experience. DXC also maintains strong ethical standards and compliance practices and supports reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

At DXC Technology, we believe strong connections and community are key to our success. Our work model prioritizes in-person collaboration while offering flexibility to support wellbeing, productivity, individual work styles, and life circumstances. We’re committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive.

title: Sr. Strategic Insights Analyst
description:
Who We Are:

Nutrabolt is a fast-growing, global active health and wellness company with a portfolio of market leading performance-oriented brands that energize and fuel active lifestyles. The company’s disruptive and innovative products compete in the Functional Beverage and Active Nutrition segments, under three consumer-loved brands: C4® (one of the fastest-growing energy drink brands in the United States and the #1 selling global pre-workout brand), XTEND® (the #1 post-workout recovery brand in the United States), and Cellucor® (an award-winning sports nutrition brand created in 2002).

Since its founding 20 years ago, Nutrabolt has set out to meet the discerning needs of performance athletes and fitness enthusiasts, while appealing beyond this core group to include consumers around the globe who are making healthy, active living a daily priority.

As a Certified Great Place to Work, Top Workplaces USA honoree, Fortune Best Workplace in Texas, and more – Nutrabolt cares deeply about our people, planet, and the communities we serve. Here, our teammates are united by our mission, and take ownership in creating a healthy workplace environment that promotes strong bodies, clear minds, and a culture of respect and belonging for all.

You will leverage a variety of data tools to develop clear and compelling insight stories that inspire action among internal stakeholders. You will bring a collaborative, growth-oriented mindset to help drive business performance and data-centric decision making.

  • Effective communication and presentation skills

  • Strong attention to detail

The Senior Director, Global Cyber Detection & Response is responsible for building and operating Danaher's global threat detection and incident response capability across our operating company portfolio. This leader owns the strategy, engineering, and day-to-day operations of the enterprise SIEM and detection platform, the detection engineering discipline, the security operations center (SOC), and the incident response function. The role is accountable for how quickly Danaher sees, understands, and stops threats across cloud, on-premises, endpoint, identity, OT/ICS, and product environments.


This position reports to the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and is part of the Global Information Security organization, located in Washington, D.C. and will be a remote role, with regular travel required to Danaher operating company and manufacturing locations globally.


Possible locations:

Israel: remote

Poland: Kraków onsite or remote


In this role, you will have the opportunity to:


  • Own Danaher's global Incident Detection & Response program, including strategy, roadmap, execution, and operational effectiveness across cloud, endpoint, identity, network, OT/ICS, and product environments, ensuring rapid threat detection, investigation, containment, eradication, recovery, and continuous improvement.
  • Lead the architecture, implementation, and operation of the enterprise detection ecosystem, including SIEM, security data lake, UEBA, SOAR, EDR/XDR, and related platforms, with accountability for platform strategy, tiering, retention, scalability, telemetry architecture, and cost governance.
  • Own the end-to-end telemetry and detection engineering lifecycle, including log source onboarding, parsing, normalization, data quality monitoring, telemetry controls, MITRE ATT&CK-aligned use case development, detection content engineering, validation, tuning, coverage measurement, and retirement of detections.
  • Build, lead, and continuously mature a global 24x7 cyber defense organization, including SOC analysts, detection engineers, incident responders, threat hunters, and automation engineers across multiple regions and management layers, while driving operational excellence, workforce development, and organizational scalability.
  • Drive adoption of AI, agentic SOC workflows, automation, and threat-informed defense capabilities, integrating threat intelligence, proactive threat hunting, automated enrichment, alert triage, investigation, response orchestration, and advanced detection techniques to improve security outcomes and analyst effectiveness.
  • Establish and govern enterprise incident response and cyber crisis management processes, including executive communications, legal and regulatory coordination, third-party incident response providers, tabletop exercises, audit support, and partnerships with operating company leadership during major incidents.
  • Define, govern, and communicate enterprise cyber defense performance, including MTTD, MTTR, ATT&CK coverage, telemetry health, analyst efficiency, false-positive reduction, backlog management, and overall program effectiveness, while partnering with OpCo CISOs, CIOs, plant leaders, product teams, executive leadership, and audit/risk committees to embed detection and response capabilities across Danaher's global businesses.

The essential requirements of the job include:


  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience) and 12+ years of information security experience, including direct ownership of security operations, detection engineering, and/or incident response within a global organization.
  • Demonstrated success standing up, migrating, or modernizing enterprise-scale SIEM environments (e.g., Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Google SecOps/Chronicle, Elastic, Panther), including data pipelines, telemetry ingestion, parsing, normalization, and detection content ownership.
  • Deep expertise across the full detection engineering lifecycle, including use case intake, backlog prioritization, MITRE ATT&CK-aligned detection development, correlation and analytic rule authoring, validation, detection-as-code, CI/CD for detections, tuning, and coverage measurement.
  • Proven leadership of a 24x7 Security Operations Center (SOC) and incident response function, including major incident command, executive communications, investigations, and coordination with legal, privacy, compliance, and regulatory stakeholders.
  • Hands-on experience with modern cyber defense technologies, including SOAR and security automation, EDR/XDR, cloud-native detection across AWS, Azure, and GCP, identity threat detection, and modern log pipeline technologies such as Cribl, Kafka, and streaming ETL.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead large-scale information security organizations through multiple layers of management, building and directing globally distributed teams across multiple regions, sites, and business environments.
  • Experience operating within highly complex, multi-country enterprises spanning 50+ countries, with responsibility for delivering consistent cybersecurity capabilities, governance, and operational outcomes across diverse geographic and organizational landscapes.

Travel, Motor Vehicle Record & Physical/Environment Requirements:

  • Ability to travel up to 20-30% of the time, including international travel to Danaher operating company, R&D, SOC, and manufacturing locations globally.

It would be a plus if you also possess previous experience in:

  • Demonstrated accomplishments applying AI and agentic SOC approaches across the log management and detection lifecycle — for example, LLM-assisted alert triage and investigation, agentic hunt and response workflows, natural-language detection authoring, automated parser generation, or AI-driven noise reduction and false-positive suppression, with measurable improvements in MTTD, MTTR, or analyst capacity.
  • Experience building or operating a modern security data lake or federated SIEM architecture that separates hot detection tier from long-term investigative and compliance storage.
  • Experience integrating detection and response across IT and OT/ICS environments, and across connected product / IoT telemetry.
  • Experience within a diversified, multi-business-unit organization operating with a decentralized business model (e.g., Danaher Business System or an equivalent operating system).
  • Professional certification such as CISSP, CISM, GCIA, GCIH, GCFA, or GNFA.
  • Experience presenting to boards, audit committees, or executive risk committees.

title: UX Researcher (MDC/AICES)
description:
SteerBridge is a modern technology company delivering innovative, mission‑focused solutions to the U.S. Government and private sector. Leveraging deep expertise in federal acquisition, digital transformation, and emerging technologies, we deliver agile, commercial‑grade capabilities that accelerate operational effectiveness and drive measurable mission success.

At the core of SteerBridge is our people—especially the veterans whose leadership, problem‑solving mindset, and commitment to excellence elevate every project we support. We don’t simply hire exceptional talent; we cultivate it, creating meaningful career pathways for veterans, military spouses, and professionals who share our passion for advancing technology and strengthening the missions we serve.

Position Overview

SteerBridge is seeking a UX Researcher with product design and prototyping capability to support the Modern Disability Claims (MDC) team and the continued development of AICES, the Artificial Intelligence Claims Evaluation System. This is a hybrid role based in the United States, with a possible remote opportunity depending on experience.

This role focuses on understanding how people review claims, navigate evidence, complete medical evaluation tasks, and respond to system-generated information. You will plan and conduct studies, synthesize findings, and translate insights into wireframes or prototype concepts that teams can evaluate with users before development. You will work alongside designers, engineers, product stakeholders, and claims and medical evaluation subject-matter experts to shape usable, accessible workflows.

AICES brings together claim information, evidence, forms, and system outputs. Research must account for the different goals, permissions, and information needs of claims reviewers, medical providers, power users, and administrators, and show whether users can trace information to its source, review or correct system-generated findings, manage exceptions, and complete their work with confidence. AICES supports medical disability examination and claims evaluation workflows, including:

  • Claims intake and information organization
  • Evidence review and source traceability
  • Medical evaluation and DBQ-related workflows
  • Review of system-generated findings and supporting information
  • Case status, exceptions, and administrative workflows

    • This work matters because these tasks affect Veterans and their claims. Success means research directly informs product decisions and delivery priorities, and the product is accessible and trustworthy, with evidence sources, system behavior, and review actions clear to the users responsible for them.

Key Responsibilities

User Research and Discovery

  • Plan and conduct qualitative and quantitative research, including interviews, contextual inquiry, surveys, and workflow analysis.
  • Study claims and medical evaluation workflows through approved access to users and representative materials, documenting constraints, handoffs, and decision points.
  • Conduct usability testing on prototypes and production workflows, including evidence review, multi-tab navigation, and administrative tasks.
  • Synthesize findings into clear, prioritized insights and recommendations that guide product decisions.
  • Develop personas or role profiles, journey maps, task flows, and workflow models when they help the team make design decisions.

    • Research-Driven Design and Prototyping

    • Translate research findings into prototype concepts that demonstrate improved claims and medical evaluation workflows.
    • Create wireframes, interaction models, and low- to mid-fidelity prototypes in Figma.
    • Collaborate with product designers to refine concepts and test whether proposed changes solve observed problems.
    • Support interaction design, information architecture, and accessibility decisions for complex, evidence-rich workflows.
    • Validate design concepts through iterative testing with the relevant user groups.

      • Systems and Product Collaboration

      • Work closely with engineers and data teams to ensure architectural patterns align with user workflows.
      • Partner with product owners and subject-matter experts to balance operational needs with technical constraints.
      • Participate in backlog refinement and design reviews.
      • Support design-to-development handoffs with clear research and workflow documentation.

        • Domain and Competitive Research

        • Conduct domain research on disability claims, medical evaluation processes, and relevant federal service workflows.
        • Analyze comparable case management and evidence review tools to inform product direction without treating competitor patterns as a substitute for user research.

Required Qualifications

  • U.S. citizenship is required for this position under applicable federal contract requirements. 3+ years of experience in UX research, human factors, or applied product research.
  • Experience planning studies, recruiting or coordinating participants, conducting sessions, and synthesizing findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Strong command of research methods, including interviews, workflow analysis, usability testing, and synthesis.
  • Ability to understand complex claims or evaluation workflows and communicate user needs clearly.
  • Experience creating research-informed prototypes or wireframes.
  • Proficiency with Figma or similar design and prototyping tools.
  • Ability to handle sensitive research materials and follow applicable project access and privacy requirements.
  • Ability to work in complex enterprise or government software environments.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to present findings to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with VA, federal health, benefits, disability claims, medical evaluation, or case management systems.
  • Experience supporting enterprise decision-support or evidence review platforms.
  • Familiarity with complex interfaces that show document sources, system-generated outputs, review status, exceptions, and user permissions.
  • Experience working with multidisciplinary teams that include engineers, product designers, subject-matter experts, and program stakeholders.
  • Experience with UX research platforms such as UserTesting, Qualtrics, or Optimal Workshop, and Agile tools such as Jira.

Job Description Summary

As part of the Department of Radiology, the Clinical Imaging Service Center (RADCORE) supports a diverse group of investigators, involving work on a wide spectrum of investigator and industry initiated clinical trials of varying complexities. Project Manager work includes overall management of research projects conducted with collaborators both internal and external to the University. Leads development of key study documents including protocol, consent forms, and CRFs, supervision of research support staff, regulatory submissions, recruitment strategy. Responsibilities may also include supporting grant writing, analyzing qualitative and quantitative data, cultivating close relationships with community partner organizations, and drafting/editing manuscripts for submission to peer-reviewed journal.

Job Description

Job Responsibilities

The Project Manager will provide project management and regulatory support and expertise associated with clinical trials for the Department of Radiology Clinical Imaging Service Center (RADCORE). The person will work closely with the RADCORE Program Manager to support a diverse group of investigators and coordinators, involving work on a wide spectrum of investigator and industry initiated clinical trials of varying complexities. Involvement will range from consulting to serving as the project manager for a study having primary responsibility with respect to execution and operational planning of the studies and accountability for results.


The Project Manager will manage/supervise the study teams assuring that each clinical trial meets expectations and that they are conducted in accordance with the specific clinical protocol as approved by the Investigator/Sponsor, study team and in accordance with all regulatory organizations. S/he will play a key role in study start-up, intake & feasibility for many studies.


The Project Manager will provide oversight and support for each study team, lead team meetings, drive study timelines, recruitment, and overall performance. S/he will generate study specific plans and documents, provide input and management of study budgets, and ensure consistent use of study tools and training materials and compliance with standard processes, policies and procedures. S/he will lead problem solving and resolution efforts, and review study status and monitor reports to identify and address possible issues. S/he will provide leadership and guidance to research personnel in their day-to-day operational activities. S/he will perform regulatory duties including regulatory oversight, regulatory submissions, and compliance checks. S/he will participate in documentation of best practices and SOPs.


Job Responsibilities

Manages project/program activities and implements protocols; develops, implements and manages work plans and timeframes in order to ensure project goals.


Communicates project/program activities to ensure clear, coordinated project related communications


Supervises assigned research support and or laboratory personnel; delegates and coordinates tasks based on developed plans


Provide technical leadership and consultation related to project/grant proposals/ manuscripts/animal protocol development, advises those associated with projects (PI) regarding project status


Oversee the delivery of patient care as defined in the study protocols and manage/supervise the study teams assuring that each clinical trial meets expectations and that they are conducted in accordance with the specific clinical protocol as approved by the Investigator/Sponsor, study team and in accordance with all regulatory organizations.


Play a key role in study start-up, intake & feasibility for many studies


Provide oversight and support for each study team, lead team meetings, drive study timelines, recruitment, and overall performance.

Other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Contingent Upon Grant Funding



Qualifications


Bachelor of Science and 3 to 5 years of experience or equivalent combination of education and experience is required. Strong planning and organizational capabilities along with attention to detail, excellent follow through and problem-solving skills necessary.

Raytheon brings the strength of more than 100 years of experience and renowned engineering expertise to meet the needs of today’s mission and stay ahead of tomorrow’s threat. The Hardware Engineering Directorate is seeking a Senior Principal Electrical Engineer with digital electronics design and analysis skills to join our team.

We are looking for candidates willing to collaborate, innovate, and team with our engineers to generate and utilize today’s cutting-edge technology to design digital electronics circuits that implement missile guidance, video and digital signal processing. Our technology base includes high-speed digital electronics, configurable logic, and homogeneous / heterogeneous multiprocessor designs.


What You Will Do

The Effector Guidance Electronics Department designs digital electronic circuit cards and electronic units which are supported from proposal through transition to production. Our systems are subject to environments ranging from the frigid, sub-zero vacuum of space to the blistering heat of the desert floor, to the high pressures of the ocean depths.


The Senior Principal Electrical Engineer is responsible for the design, analysis, simulation, test, and integration of digital electronic modules and/or CCAs for missile applications. The candidate should be experienced in all aspects of circuit card design including hardware designs with processors, FPGAs, memory, and industry interfaces, such as PCIe, Ethernet, I2C, SPI, and UART.

  • Typically requires a Bachelors Degree in Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) and a minimum of 10 years of prior relevant experience
  • Minimum of ten (10) years engineering digital circuit design experience
  • Experience in the development and design of electronic circuit designs, and/or multi-assembly system/unit design

Qualifications We Prefer

  • Experience in taking design concepts from block diagram or requirements level to development of complete hardware designs, with verification via test and integration
  • Experience with PCB design process and expertise with design tools (schematic capture) to analyze and simulate designs prior to hardware execution
  • Experience using Mentor Graphics Design Creation (Siemens EDA) tools: DxDesigner, xDX Designer VX, and/or Expedition
  • Experience using PCB electronic circuit design software: HyperLynx signal integrity, power integrity and analog simulation, and/or Xpedition Enterprise (xPCB)

What We Offer

Our values drive our actions, behaviors, and performance with a vision for a safer, more connected world. At RTX we value: Safety, Trust, Respect, Accountability, Collaboration, and Innovation.

The Hardware Engineering Directorate is seeking an Electrical Engineer II with digital electronics design and analysis skills to join our team.

The Digital Hardware Engineer II is responsible for the design, analysis, simulation, test, and integration of digital electronic modules and/or CCAs for missile applications.   • Experience in taking design concepts from block diagram or requirements level to development of complete hardware designs, with verification via test and integration
  • Experience with PCB design process and expertise with design tools (schematic capture) to analyze and simulate designs prior to hardware execution
  • Experience using Mentor Graphics Design Creation (Siemens EDA) tools: DxDesigner, xDX Designer VX, and/or Expedition
  • Experience using PCB electronic circuit design software: HyperLynx signal integrity, power integrity and analog simulation, and/or Xpedition Enterprise (xPCB)

Our values drive our actions, behaviors, and performance with a vision for a safer, more connected world. At RTX we value: Safety, Trust, Respect, Accountability, Collaboration, and Innovation.

HEABC leads and supports the strategic planning related to human resources and labour relations on behalf of British Columbia’s publicly funded health employers. HEABC is responsible for negotiating provincial agreements for 190,000 unionized health care employees including nurses, physician residents, ambulance paramedics, health science professionals, and more.

HEABC Medical Staff Services leads a coordinated approach to the negotiation of provincial and local medical staff agreements and provides expert advice to health system partners on their relationships with medical staff. Join our highly talented team in a culture of learning, innovation, and visionary thinking. Join our highly talented team in a culture of learning, innovation, and visionary thinking.

The successful candidate may be permitted to work in a hybrid model (combination of in-office and flexible work location) and will live within commuting distance of our Vancouver office.

For more information, visit

OPPORTUNITY:


Reporting to the Director, Research and Analysis, the Economics and Policy Analyst (the Analyst) performs technical research work; carries out interpretive and analytical activities; engages in, and conducts complex costing work for, physician contract and Physician Main Agreement negotiations; provides economics assessments, evaluates and develops policy options related to the delivery of and compensation of physician services; prepares and presents reports, and provides advice to the Director to identify potential areas of research, objectives, methodologies and requirements.

This position requires initiative, creativity, critical thinking, attention to detail, quantitative skills, proficiency in analytical methods, and outstanding presentation and writing skills. In this role, you will partner with a wide range of system partners, including senior staff of the Ministry of Health, health authorities and other health system partners. The ideal candidate will have a passion for conducting research that supports evidence-based policy and the diplomacy to develop and maintain strong relationships.

Responsibilities include:


  • Fosters the development of partnerships between HEABC, health authorities, the Ministry of Health and other health system partners on projects related to the delivery of and compensation for medical services.
  • Co-develops materials (e.g. briefing notes and presentations) for and/or participates in the meeting program for the Provincial Medical Services Executive Council and other Ministry of Health/Health Authority committees where evidence and materials are required to support local or Provincial-level discussion, policy and decision-making.
  • Recommends the design of and carries out rigorous methodologies for literature reviews, environmental scans, quantitative and qualitative research.
  • Manages data collection and designs databases; works with very large data sets and multiple data sources – cleans, organizes, link, and structure data.
  • Develops, analyses, and interprets various statistical and economic data, research studies, wage and salary surveys, and policy options to support decision-makers with evidence-based, statistically supported, and methodologically consistent advice.
  • Prepares related presentations, data visualizations, studies, and/or reports that effectively communicate the results of research and analysis, to be used by HEABC and /or MOH.


Required Experience & Knowledge:


A master’s degree in economics, statistics, mathematics, business, or a health or social science discipline and at least three (3) years of related research or policy experience, preferably in the health care sector;


  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint;
  • Experience with electronic research databases and analytical software; with proficiency in one or more of the following analytical tools: SAS, R, STATA, Tableau, SQL, or related.
  • Outstanding interpersonal, problem-solving, and written and verbal communication skills.

Typical Hiring Range: $90,770 to $113,462

title: Child Facilitator
description:

In addition, we support people experiencing unemployment, addiction and family challenges. We continually adapt and innovate to meet emerging needs and live out our mission, vision and values of hope, service, dignity and stewardship. As a faith- and values-based organization, we hire and serve people of all backgrounds and walks of life - there is a place for everyone to belong here.

Mission Statement

The Salvation Army exists to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in the communities of our world.

Job Description:

This position develops, implements, and facilitates program for children, ages 6 to 12, ensuring activities are provided in a safe fun and inclusive environment

  • Ensures that all resources are inventoried and organized.

  • Participates in program evaluation and assessments.

  • May assist manager in researching and developing future community partnerships.

  • Accumulate relevant programs statistics.

  • Always maintains client confidentiality.

  • Participates in program staff meetings.

  • Attends other meetings as requested by the supervisor.

Annual Responsibilities:

  • Conducts annual review of program curriculum and makes recommendations for enhancements or changes to ensure continued relevance.

  • Assists with preparation of annual programs statistics.

  • This is a full-time position at 40 hours per week and hours may vary based on peak seasons.

  • Located at Community Family Resource Centre in Forest Lawn SE.

  • Deals with typical child behavior

  • Completed a two-year college diploma in a child development or related field.

  • Standard first aid certificate with level C CPR from an Alberta approved provider

  • Incumbents with a social work diploma or degree must be registered with the Alberta College of Social Workers.

  • At least three years of prior related experience in facilitating a program for children.

  • Knowledgeable about legislation regarding reporting of child abuse/neglect.

  • Familiar with current educational resources for children.

  • Uses best methods/practices for teaching.

  • Is aware of various learning styles: visual, auditory and kinesthetic. Adds elements in program that supports all learning styles.

  • Incorporates variety of art mediums into program.

Skills and Capabilities:

  • Proficient in MS Office 365 (Outlook, Excel, TEAMS, Word, etc.)

  • Enjoys interacting with a wide range of children from different backgrounds.

  • Aware of legal responsibilities regarding reporting of child abuse and neglect.

  • Demonstrates healthy boundaries with youth and children.

  • Promotes respect for cultural diversity.

  • Team player who makes positive contributions to the team and supports coworkers.

  • Strong sense of integrity and confidentiality with professional ethics and a balanced sense of fairness and flexibility.

Compensation:

Placement in the salary range will be based on factors such as market conditions, internal equity, and candidate experience, skills, and qualifications relevant to the role.

    Being You

We focus on ensuring all Kyndryls feel included and we welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. title: FT Inbound Freight Handler
description:
As a FT Inbound Freight Handler, you will load and unload freight onto and off of equipment, as well as assist in the recouping of damaged freight.

Prepare, sweep, inspect and cleans trailer(s) before loading freight. Use safe lifting techniques to properly load and unload freight. Select and use proper freight handling equipment to load and unload freight. Such equipment may include forklifts with appropriate hardware, hand trucks, drum trucks, pallet jacks, rollers, and any other available equipment to move, load, arrange, rearrange, and unload freight. Weigh and dimension shipments to ensure proper classification, freight rating, and safe handling. Plan cube utilization and proper weight distribution when loading freight. Count and inspect the condition of freight, documenting any shortages or damage. Review freight bills for special instructions. Check manifests for existing exceptions and check the label and the destination code on manifests against freight bills. Check for special instructions, weight distributions on headloads, and check headloads against the freight bills when loading freight. Verify the hazardous material product description, determine any discrepancies in the paperwork, and verify proper placarding when loading hazardous material. Properly block and brace freight to prevent shifting during transport.

For this role, we prefer you have a High School Diploma or GED. You must have the ability to satisfactorily pass a background check and an alcohol and drug test. We would prefer for you to have prior experience as a Forklift Operator, Dock or Warehouse Worker, or Material Handler. We would also prefer you to have previously held a Forklift Certification. title: Organizational Change Leader
description:
Union Tank Car Company & Procor

As a part of the global industrial organization Marmon Holdings—which is backed by Berkshire Hathaway—you’ll be doing things that matter, leading at every level, and winning a better way. We’re committed to making a positive impact on the world, providing you with diverse learning and working opportunities, and fostering a culture where everyone’s empowered to be their best.

Must be eligible to work in Chicago, IL, without visa sponsorship

LOCATION REQUIREMENT - MUST RESIDE WITHIN COMMUTING DISTANCE OF OUR CHICAGO HQ OFFICE FOR A HYBRID (MINIMUM 2 DAYS/WEEK) IN OFFICE ENVIRONMENT.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Organizational Change Leader will lead the people‑side of change for our enterprise‑wide ERP implementation, Organization Integration & Optimization and additional organization-wide change initiatives as assigned. Over the next three years, this role will drive stakeholder alignment, readiness, and adoption for significant changes in systems, processes, automation/technology, and roles & responsibilities. In partnership with the ERP program, HR, IT, Finance, Operations, and business leadership, the OCM will define and execute a comprehensive change strategy that minimizes disruption, accelerates proficiency, and realizes business case benefits.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Enterprise ERP Transformation

  • Change Strategy & Governance: Lead the change workstream for the ERP program; establish governance, tollgates, and cadence with the PMO and SI partner; integrate change plans with program plan, cutover, and hyper care.
  • Stakeholder & Sponsorship: Map stakeholders; create a sponsor roadmap; coach executives and people leaders to model and reinforce change.
  • Change Impact & Readiness: Conduct impact assessments for processes, policies, roles, org structure, and competencies; drive mitigation actions and readiness plans.
  • Communications: Build an executive and field‑level communications plan (town halls, leader toolkits, FAQs, short videos, Yammer/Teams posts, “day‑in‑the‑life” narratives).
  • Training & Enablement: Partner with HR/L&D to run training needs analysis; define curricula, learning paths, and train‑the‑trainer; coordinate with LMS and site leads; produce job aids and quick‑reference guides.
  • Change Network & Super Users: Stand up and lead a change agent/super‑user network across functions and sites to support testing, UAT, and go‑live adoption.
  • Cutover & Hypercare: Prepare the organization for cutover; stand up command‑center routines; monitor adoption, sentiment, and issue trends post‑go‑live; close feedback loops.
  • Adoption & Benefits Realization: Define and track adoption KPIs (e.g., role‑based training completion, proficiency curves, reduction in manual workarounds, utilization of standard processes), and partner with Finance/PMO to connect to the ERP business case.

Organizational Transformation (Integration & Optimization)

  • “One Company” Ways of Working: Drive harmonization of processes and role expectations; support leader assimilation and team norms across the integrated platform. (Aligned to our centralization and ERP journey.)
  • Org Design & Role/Responsibility Clarity: Partner with HR and business leaders on org design implications, role mapping, RACIs, and job description updates; support change‑related staffing transitions and communications.
  • Culture & Leadership Enablement: Build leader playbooks and facilitated sessions to reinforce desired behaviors, decision rights, and cross‑BU collaboration.
  • Readiness & Risk Management: Maintain an integrated change risk register for the integration; escalate and resolve resistance hotspots and capacity constraints.

Program Ways of Working

  • Data‑Driven Change: Stand up dashboards (e.g., Power BI) for readiness, sentiment, and adoption; derive insights and recommended actions.
  • Co‑Creation & Field Engagement: Use design‑thinking workshops, journey maps, and “voice of the user” forums to shape solutions and reduce resistance.
  • Compliance & Policy Alignment: Identify policy/process changes needed for ERP standardization; coordinate approvals and rollout plans.
  • External Partner Management: Coordinate with the systems integrator and change/learning vendors; ensure deliverables meet our standards and are practical for field adoption.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, IT, Organizational Development or equivalent
  • 10 years in organizational change management leading large‑scale transformations, including ERP or other enterprise-wide Technology Platform implementation required (SAP, Oracle, Microsoft, Infor, Workday, etc.)
  • Proven experience with multi‑site operations and business unit integration or centralization programs.
  • Mastery of core OCM methods (e.g., Prosci/ADKAR, stakeholder analysis, impact assessment, change planning, communications, training/enablement, benefits realization).
  • Exceptional facilitation, executive influence, and storytelling skills; ability to translate complex program changes into practical field impacts.
  • Strong program skills (planning, risk management, interdependency tracking) and analytics (readiness/adoption dashboards).
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft 365/Teams/SharePoint; comfort partnering with PMO and SI partners.
  • Ability to travel: ~15–25%
  • Hybrid work arrangement: minimum two days per week in the Chicago office.

Preferred

  • Prosci®, CCMP (ACMP), or equivalent certification; PMP and/or Agile experience a plus.
  • Background in asset‑intensive, manufacturing, leasing, or field service environments.
  • Experience establishing change networks and standing up command‑center routines for major go‑lives.

title: Order Management Specialist
description:
This position will be fully remote and can be hired anywhere in the continental U.S.


Optiv + ClearShark is seeking an entry-level/junior Order Management Specialist to support the accurate and compliant processing of sales orders across our federal and commercial cybersecurity business. Reporting to the Senior Director of Sales Operations, this position is responsible for reviewing, quality-assuring (QA), and activating sales orders, coordinating with internal sales teams to resolve order discrepancies, and tracking order fulfillment through to delivery. This is an excellent opportunity for a detail-oriented professional to build a career in sales operations within a fast-paced government contracting environment.


How you’ll make an impact

  • Review and validate incoming sales orders against customer purchase orders (POs), OEM/Distributor cost quotes, and applicable contract terms and conditions.
  • Ensure orders comply with relevant FAR/DFARS clauses and contract-specific requirements prior to activation.
  • Perform quality assurance checks to confirm pricing, part numbers, quantities, and contract references are accurate and complete before releasing orders.
  • Activate validated sales orders in accordance with established sales operations procedures.
  • Partner with the Sales and Inside Sales teams to identify, research, and reconcile order discrepancies, including pricing mismatches, quote variances, and incomplete PO documentation.
  • Serve as a point of contact for order-related questions, escalating complex issues to the Senior Director of Sales Operations as needed.
  • Fulfillment Tracking and Delivery Documentation
  • After a PO is submitted to the Distributor/OEM, track order fulfillment status to ensure timely and complete delivery.
  • Ensure customers receive required documentation, including proof of delivery/shipment, license keys, and other deliverables.
  • Upload and maintain proof of delivery (POD) and related documentation in the Salesforce (SF) repository, ensuring records are accurate, complete, and audit-ready.
  • Work with the Sales Operations Team to ensure Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and order management processes remain current, streamlined, and consistently followed.
  • Recommend improvements to enhance order accuracy, cycle time, and compliance.
  • This position may require after-hours support during peak business periods, including end of month, end of quarter, and federal fiscal year end (FFYE), to ensure timely order processing and fulfillment.

What we’re looking for

  • High School Diploma or Equivalent Experience
  • 0-2 years of experience in order management, sales operations, procurement, contract administration, or a related field.
  • Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy and data integrity.
  • Ability to work collaboratively across sales, operations, and finance teams.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel, Outlook, Word).
  • Exposure to or basic understanding of FAR/DFARS and federal contract terms and conditions.
  • Experience with Salesforce (SF) or a comparable CRM/order management system.
  • Familiarity with OEM/Distributor quoting and procurement processes within the IT or cybersecurity reseller environment.
  • Interest in growing a career in sales operations or contract management.

What you can expect from Optiv

  • Work/life balance

  • Professional training resources

  • Creative problem-solving and the ability to tackle unique, complex projects

  • Volunteer Opportunities. “Optiv Chips In” encourages employees to volunteer and engage with their teams and communities.

  • The ability and technology necessary to productively work remotely/from home (where applicable)
