title: Clinical Dietitian II or III
description:
Better at Work. Better at Life.

When you work at St. Jude, you’ll join a highly collaborative work culture that inspires you every day to be your best. With opportunities for learning and growth, you can shape a career path that is right for you while also enjoying all the benefits and stability of working for a world-class institution. This includes work-life balance with generous paid time-off and on-campus conveniences that make life a little easier. Join us and you’ll quickly see why St. Jude is consistently ranked by our employees on Glassdoor as a “Best Place to Work.”

The Clinical Dietitan II or III will provide age-appropriate nutrition care through expert practice, education, consultation, research, and leadership. Participates as a member of the interdisciplinary health care team; serves as a resource for the Medical and Nursing staff, ancillary team members and others, as appropriate, outside of the institution. Utilizes clinical practice and knowledge of advanced pediatric oncology nutrition principles to provide evidence-based nutrition care. Participates in institutional and professional activities to promote the profession, the department and the institution. Performs other duties as assigned or directed to meet the objectives of the department and the organization.


Clinical Dietitan II


Job Responsibilities:

  • Develop and deliver medical nutrition therapy to patients based on patient needs and standard processes.
  • Assess nutritional status, determine nutritional requirements, and set appropriate goals according to established standards.
  • Institute appropriate type of nutrition support, evaluate outcome of medical nutritional therapy,
  • Adjust medical nutrition therapy by recommending and initiating appropriate changes in delivery of nutrients to achieve established outcomes.
  • Provide appropriate nutrition intervention and education/ instruction to patients/ families.
  • Participate in quality control/quality assurance activities within department.
  • Participate in nutrition research and/ or projects.
  • Collaborate with interdisciplinary healthcare teams to ensure integrated care.
  • Serve as a nutrition resource, educator, and consultant for patient’s health care professionals, students, and the community.
  • Perform other duties as assigned to meet the goals and objectives of the department and institution.
  • Maintain regular and predictable attendance.


Minimum Education and/or Training:

  • Master's degree in nutrition or a related field including an ACEND-approved dietetic internship required.


Minimum Experience:

  • Minimum Experience: 3+ years of experience in clinical dietetics required.
  • Clinical experience in an pediatrics/hospital setting preferred.
  • Proven performance in earlier/ comparable role.


Licensure, Registration and/or Certification Required by Law:

  • Dietitian/Nutritionist License (LDN-TN) by State of Tennessee Division of Health-Related Boards required.
  • Registered as a Dietitian/Nutritionist (LC: CDRAND-RD) by the Commission on Dietetic Registration for the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics required.

Licensure, Registration and/or Certification Required by SJCRH Only:

  • Certification in Nutrition Support by the American Society of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition preferred.
  • Board Certification as a Specialist in Pediatric Nutrition by the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics preferred.
  • Board Certification as a Specialist in Oncology Nutrition by the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics preferred.
  • International Board-Certified Lactation Consultant by the International Board of Lactation Consultant Examiners preferred.
  • Certified Clinical Research Associate by the Society of Clinical Research Associates preferred.




Clinical Dietitan III

Job Responsibilities:

  • Develop and deliver medical nutrition therapy to patients based on patient needs and standard processes.
  • Assess nutritional status, determine nutritional requirements, and set appropriate goals according to established standards.
  • Institute appropriate type of nutrition support, evaluate outcome of medical nutritional therapy,
  • Adjust medical nutrition therapy by recommending and initiating appropriate changes in delivery of nutrients to achieve established outcomes.
  • Provide appropriate nutrition intervention and education/ instruction to patients/ families.
  • Execute quality control/quality assurance activities within department.
  • Participate and support researchers with designing and conducting research and projects (including development of nutrition component of treatment protocols).
  • Collaborate with interdisciplinary healthcare teams to ensure integrated care.
  • Serve as a nutrition resource, educator, and consultant for patient’s health care professionals, students, and the community.
  • Collaborate with departmental administration to support execution of projects/ operations.
  • Serve as the departmental representative for a recognized nutrition-related committee/ board.
  • Perform other duties as assigned to meet the goals and objectives of the department and institution.
  • Maintain regular and predictable attendance.

Minimum Education and/or Training:

  • Master's degree in nutrition or a related field including an ACEND-approved dietetic internship required.

Minimum Experience:

  • 5+ years of experience in clinical dietetics required and 3+ years of experience in pediatrics or oncology.
  • Proven performance in earlier/ comparable role.

Licensure, Registration and/or Certification Required by Law:

  • (LC: LDN-TN) Licensure by the State of Tennessee Division of Health Related Boards as a Dietitian/Nutritionist required
  • (LC: CDRAND-RD) Registered as a Dietitian/Nutritionist by the Commission on Dietetic Registration for the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics required

  • (LC: NBNSC-NS) Certification in Nutrition Support by the National Board of Nutrition Support established by American Society of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (ASPEN) preferred

  • (LC: LACCON) International Board Certified Lactation Consultant by the International Board of Lactation Consultant Examiners preferred
  • (LC: SOCRA) Certified Clinical Research Associate by the Society of Clinical Research Associates preferred

Compensation

In recognition of certain U.S. state and municipal pay transparency laws, St. Jude is including a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This is an estimate offered in good faith and a specific salary offer takes into account factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. title: Journeyman Wireman
description:
Join Golden Valley Electric Association as a full-time Journeyman Wireman at our Healy, Alaska, power plant! This is a hands-on opportunity to install, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair electrical wiring, controls, instrumentation, and equipment that support reliable power generation.

In this role, you'll work with electrical and process control systems, transformers, protective relays, fiber optics, test equipment, and other critical plant systems. The position works a 7-day-on, 7-day-off schedule, 12 hours per day, with additional hours as required.

This bargaining-unit position offers competitive pay of $64.87 per hour, per IBEW Agreement, along with benefits including Retirement/401(k), Health Insurance, Life Insurance, Short- and Long-Term Disability, Paid Leave, Flexible Spending, and Wellness Benefits. Bring your electrical expertise to GVEA and help keep Interior Alaska powered!

A LITTLE ABOUT US

GVEA is an electric cooperative that owns and maintains 3,491 miles of transmission and distribution lines, 35 substations, and 9 generating facilities. Our system is interconnected with Fort Wainwright, Eielson AFB, Fort Greely, Clear Space Force Station, the University of Alaska-Fairbanks, and all electric utilities in the Alaska Railbelt, which extends from Homer to Fairbanks. Powering the Interior of Alaska, GVEA contributes to the economic, environmental, and social viability of our communities.

YOUR ROLE AS THE JOURNEYMAN WIREMAN

As a Journeyman Wireman at Golden Valley Electric Association, you will install, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair electrical wiring, controls, instrumentation, and equipment at the Healy Power Plant. You will work with a variety of electrical and control systems that are essential to safe and reliable plant operations.

In this role, you will test and repair electrical equipment, transformers, reclosers, protective relays, and controls; install and test fiber optic cable; and work with instrumentation and process control systems. You will also support new construction by installing conduit, wiring, electrical services, lighting, and power distribution equipment.

WHAT YOU NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL

Candidates should have strong electrical knowledge and hands-on experience installing, maintaining, and troubleshooting electrical systems. Journeyman Wireman certification is required, along with four or more years of experience and/or four years of apprenticeship training.

Knowledge and skills required for the position include:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Formal electrical training; extensive work experience may count toward a portion of the educational requirements.
  • Journeyman Wireman certification.
  • Four or more years of experience and/or four years of apprenticeship training.
  • Valid Alaska driver's license with an excellent driving record.
  • Valid First Aid card or ability to obtain one within 30 days of hire.
  • Knowledge of electrical theory, circuits, and power distribution.

If you think this job is a fit for what you are looking for, great! We're excited to meet you!

title: Ministry Leader in Training – Aspiring Leader Program
description:
Feel called to ministry? Come spend the next season being trained, mentored, and developed by experienced Adult & Teen Challenge leaders while gaining hands-on experience in nearly every area of ministry.

Adult & Teen Challenge of Texas is looking for Aspiring Leaders who have a heart to serve and a desire to grow into future ministry leadership.

This is much more than an internship. It is an immersive ministry leadership development program designed to give aspiring leaders hands-on experience while being intentionally trained, mentored, and developed by experienced Adult & Teen Challenge leaders.

Interns serve directly under our Department Heads and ministry leadership, rotating through key areas of Adult & Teen Challenge—including Admissions, Education, Development, Vocational/Work Experience, Maintenance, Kitchen, Campus Business, and Administration. The goal is to learn how the ministry operates from the ground up while developing the spiritual character and practical leadership skills needed for vocational ministry. This matches the internship's stated purpose of training future vocational ministers through mentoring, supervision, department rotations, and opportunities to participate in leadership.

Aspiring Leaders will also have opportunities to participate in monthly Coordinator Trainings, specialized ministry training, and additional training provided through our Corporate Office, while receiving ongoing development from campus leadership.

For individuals who desire a future with Adult & Teen Challenge, the internship can provide valuable preparation for future ministry opportunities. Completion of the internship does not guarantee employment, but the program is intentionally designed to develop individuals for vocational ministry and leadership.

This is a volunteer ministry internship, not a paid employment position. Interns receive room and board, meals, supervision, transportation to ATCOT events and special group outings, and access to most campus facilities. When an intern does not have outside support, the campus may also assist with basic essentials within reason.



Requirements

Requirements

We are looking for individuals who:

  • Have a genuine desire to pursue vocational Christian ministry and leadership.
  • Have a teachable spirit and a willingness to serve.
  • Want to be trained, mentored, challenged, and developed by experienced ministry leaders.
  • Are willing to serve under Department Heads and learn multiple areas of ministry.
  • Desire to grow spiritually and develop practical leadership skills.
  • Are willing to participate in biblical studies, ministry training, department rotations, weekly development meetings, outreach, and other required activities.
  • Are willing to make the required commitment to the internship program.
  • If applying from outside ATCOT, can provide at least two written recommendations, preferably from a pastor and mentor.


Benefits

Benefits / What You'll Receive

  • Hands-on ministry leadership development
  • Direct mentoring and training from Department Heads and campus leadership
  • Experience serving in multiple departments throughout Adult & Teen Challenge
  • Monthly Coordinator Leadership Training
  • Specialized training through our Corporate Office
  • Biblical and discipleship training
  • Opportunities to develop leadership, communication, ministry, and administrative skills
  • Exposure to the day-to-day operation of a residential recovery ministry
  • Opportunities for outreach, church ministry, evangelism, and missions
  • Room and board provided
  • Meals provided
  • Transportation to ATCOT events and special group outings
  • Assistance with basic essentials when needed and approved

The Site Facilitator serves as the primary on-site contact during assigned shifts, overseeing facility operations, responding to incidents in accordance with established protocols, and coordinating with campus partners as needed.

Facility Operations


  • Oversee the day-to-day operation of the assigned campus site during evening hours.

  • Assist campus visitors with directions and general information.
  • Utilize the CSN website and internal resources to locate faculty/staff for contact information and college program details.

Safety and Emergency Response

  • Notify appropriate on-call staff and emergency personnel, including Security, Custodial Services, and Operations & Maintenance, when situations arise.
  • Follow established emergency protocols and coordinate with Campus Life leadership, and University Police Services, and campus as necessary.

Program Support


  • Support Campus Life programming, student engagement initiatives, and special events scheduled during evening hours.
  • Assist with extended-hour operations of the Coyote Cupboard to support student basic needs access.
  • Collaborate with Learning Center staff, as applicable, to support programming and student resource initiatives aligned with Campus Life services.
  • Provide access to Lactation Rooms for nursing mothers, study rooms, and other specialty rooms.

Communication and Reporting


  • Always Represent CSN and Campus Life in a professional manner.
  • Report urgent incidents or concerns immediately to the Supervisor via telephone.
  • Report site activity daily

Other Duties


  • Perform other duties as assigned to support campus operations and student services.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities


  • Knowledge of or ability to learn CSN policies, procedures, and emergency protocols.
  • Strong interpersonal, communication, and customer service skills.
  • Ability to work independently and make sound decisions during evening operations.
  • Ability to remain calm and professional in emergency or high-pressure situations.

Interested applicants are invited to join Atrium Health Levine Cancer’s physics practice working alongside a dynamic care team. Atrium Health Levine Cancer (AHLC) provides patients with access to nationally renowned physicians and state-of-the-art treatments at 25+ cancer care locations across the Carolinas, including 10 radiation therapy centers in the Greater Charlotte, NC area.


Atrium Health is recruiting a staff Medical Physicist to support clinical services at our Northern Area radiation therapy clinics (AHLC Cabarrus, AHLC Stanly and AHLC University City). These facilities collectively feature 2 Varian Truebeams (Cabarrus), one Varian Clinac iX (University) and one Trilogy linac (Stanly), all with Surface Image Guidance setup and motion management systems. The treatment planning system is Varian Eclipse (v16.1) and ARIA is the oncology EMR. Each clinic has a CT scanner to support clinical simulations


The interested candidate would join a team of 5 other medical physicists, 5 dosimetrists and 4 physicians dedicated to supporting the Northern Area clinics. Atrium Health’s Charlotte clinics are home to 50+ physicists, dosimetrists and medical physics assistants dedicated to supporting external beam and modalities across our network.


The 7 other Greater Charlotte-region Atrium Health Levine Cancer Radiation Therapy clinics are equipped with CT Simulators (GE/Philips), as well as Varian treatment planning (Eclipse v16.1), EMR (ARIA 15.6/16.1) and Clinac/TrueBeam treatment delivery systems, with one clinic equipped with RayStation (v2023B) TPS, Mosaiq EMR and an Elekta Infinity linear accelerator. AHLC’s Charlotte-area clinics have active SBRT and SRS programs and employ Surface Image Guidance Technology in all facilities. Our network of clinics also includes the Proton and Advanced Radiation Therapy Center which features the 2-state region’s only proton beam delivery system, Gamma Knife-based SRS and an active radiopharmaceutical therapy program. MIM Maestro image management software including AI contouring tools is also utilized. A full complement of QA tools and technologies are available. Active clinical projects include knowledge-based planning techniques, AI contouring, clinical implementation of Cherenkov radiation in radiotherapy and QA standardization using a cloud-based platform.


Additionally, our Charlotte area clinics currently host trainees from the Carolinas College of Health Sciences in radiation therapy and medical dosimetry. Physicists also serve as mentors in the joint Atrium Health/Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist CAMPEP-approved medical physics residency program. In 2025, the Charlotte campus of the Wake Forest University School of Medicine opened with its inaugural class of medical students. It is anticipated that opportunities for academic faculty physicist roles will be available to interested and appropriate candidates.


Interested candidates will join a collaborative environment where physicists work across facilities on projects impacting patients' network-wide.



Major Responsibilities:

  • Performs delivery of non-standard, standard and complicated treatment planning and techniques which may include high dose radiation (HDR), low dose radiation (LDR) and stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS). Performs radiation surveys of patients exposed to radioactive sources; regularly performs radiation surveys of treatment rooms.
  • Calibrates various therapy machines, measures instruments against national standards, and measures therapy beam data for treatment planning purposes. Leads and facilitates the troubleshooting process, works collaboratively with Medical Engineers. Operates and performs quality assurance (QA) on equipment as required.
  • Writes specifications and commissions therapy equipment and accessories and designs new techniques and ancillary equipment. Performs and oversees commissioning and acceptance testing for therapies and accessories, and for standardizing equipment calibration.
  • Collaborates with other senior staff to develop and maintain a QA program for departmental treatment modalities and imaging devices. Works with Physicians to gather data, analyze outcomes and develop new processes and protocols. Develops, implements and oversees the department radiation safety policies.
  • Tracks and monitors data or parameters directly affecting patient dose and verifies algorithms used in pertinent dose calculations. Enters and validates data in treatment planning systems. Performs data collection and provides benchmark information for Institute, National and International protocols; performs physics measurements and oversight for special procedures and leads special programs as assigned.
  • Consults with Radiation Oncologists and Physicians on target delineation, modeling and treatment planning.
  • Establishes processes and procedures for acquiring high quality images for treatment planning and treatment delivery; monitors and measures the performance of all imaging equipment.
  • Develops and implements new techniques for treatment delivery, and assists with designing and modifying radiotherapy treatment rooms to incorporate radiation protection standards required by national protocols; makes recommendations regarding acquisition and implementation for major equipment and supportive technology.
  • Provides education lectures to staff therapists and associated allied staff and provides mandatory radiation safety training. Assists with accreditation process, departmental QA activities, and radiation safety committee as assigned; leads the development of a new competency or assists in completion of competencies for other staff.
  • Ensures compliance with all state and federal regulating and accrediting bodies.
  • Must be able to demonstrate knowledge and skills necessary to provide care appropriate to the age of the patients served. Must demonstrate knowledge of the principles of growth and development over the life span and possess the ability to assess data reflective of the patient's status and interpret the appropriate information needed to identify each patient's requirements relative to his/her age-specific needs, and to provide the care needed as described in the department's policies and procedures. Age-specific information is developed further in the departmental job standards.


Licensure, Registration, and/or Certification Required:

  • Medical Physicist certification issued by the American Board of Medical Physics (ABMP), or
  • Medical Physicist (CMP-ABR) certification issued by The American Board of Radiology (ABR), or
  • Medical Physicist (CMP-CCPM) certification issued by The Canadian College of Physicists in Medicine (CCPM).


Education Required:

  • Master's Degree in Medical Physics or related field.


Experience Required:

  • Typically requires 3 years of experience in in a Medical Physicist Oncology position.


Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Required:

  • Advanced knowledge of treatment units and simulators and awareness of treatment unit's limitations in clinical situations.
  • Advanced knowledge of acceptance testing, commissioning and calibration of linacs, simulators and brachytherapy sources, clinical dosimetry of external beams and implant sources, patient setup, computerized treatment planning for special procedures that may include: HDR, LDR, total body irradiation (TBI), stereotactic radiosurgery, stereotactic radiotherapy, gamma knife and cyberknife.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to communicate effectively with physicians, staff, patients and their families.
  • Excellent problem solving abilities and analytical skills to compare data.


Physical Requirements and Working Conditions:

  • Must lift up to 20 lbs. frequently and up to 50 lbs. occasionally.
  • May push up to 500 lbs. 50 to 200 feet.
  • Exposed to mechanical, electrical, and radiation hazards.
  • Operates all equipment necessary to perform the job.
  • Exposed to a normal office environment.

title: Powder Coater
description:
Powder Coater

Responsibilities:

  • Ensure product quality meets standards by frequently checking work.
  • Examining finished products for uniformity, defects and adherence to client specifications.
  • Maintenance of the spray gun parts and booths according to instructions.

Required Skills:

title: Supervisor, Maintenance Tech
description:
Tempur Sealy. Iconic brands. Storied history. Industry-leading innovation.

Tempur Sealy is committed to improving the sleep of more people, every night, all around the world. As a leading designer, manufacturer, distributor, and retailer of bedding products worldwide, we know how crucial a good night of sleep is to overall health and wellness. Utilizing over a century of knowledge and industry-leading innovation, we deliver award-winning products that provide breakthrough sleep solutions to consumers in over 100 countries. Our highly recognized brands include Tempur-Pedic®, Sealy® and Stearns & Foster®. We hire people who have a passion for helping others find their best night’s sleep. No matter what stage of your career, you can build your future at Tempur Sealy!

What You’ll Do:

  • Maintain responsibility for the installation, start-up, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of all mechanical and electrical processes used in the manufacture of mattresses, mattress components, and similar bedding products. Such equipment may include sewing equipment, foam fabrication equipment, motors, pumps, conveyors, belts, fans, etc.
  • Manage and maximize the output of plant equipment used in production, functional longevity, and aesthetic of the products.
  • Plan, delegate, and perform work that requires a thorough knowledge of electrical and mechanical theories and principles, written specifications, local and national electrical codes, properties of various materials, and the principles of operation and application for electronic equipment.
  • Directly manage all maintenance staff, contractors, OEM’s to ensure safety, timely production, and completion of their projects.
  • Collaborate with Plant Director and Department Supervisors to ensure successful accomplishment of the site’s production needs.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Salary Range: $70,000 - $95,000/Year


Requirements:

  • A bachelor’s degree in mechanical or electrical engineering (or equivalent experience).
  • 2 years of experience with a demonstrated understanding of manufacturing, mechanical, and electrical systems, including: hydraulic systems, HVAC, low- and high-pressure-pumps, open and closed loop piping systems, and PLC’s.
  • Supervisory experience is preferred but not required.
  • Demonstrated experience with computer maintenance management systems.
  • Arc flash, HAZWOPER, and forklift operator’s certifications, or the ability to obtain the certifications.

title: Technical Product Owner
description:
Job Description

Purpose of the role

To collaborate with product owners and other technical teams involved in the product development process and utilise their knowledge of the bank’s technologies to enact the vision defined in the product roadmap.

Accountabilities

  • Provision of subject matter expertise to support the collaboration between the product owner and the technical side of product development.
  • Support the development and implementation of the product strategy and vision defined in the product roadmap and communicate them with the relevant stakeholders and the development team.
  • Collaboration with internal stakeholders to gather and prioritise product requirements and features based on business value and feasibility that are well defined, measurable and secure.
  • Development and implementation of assessments to ensure continuous testing and improvement of product quality and performance.
  • Monitoring of product performance to identify opportunities for optimisation that meets the banks performance standards.
  • Stay abreast of the latest industry technology trends and technologies, to evaluate and adopt new approaches to improve product development and delivery.

Assistant Vice President Expectations

  • To advise and influence decision making, contribute to policy development and take responsibility for operational effectiveness. Collaborate closely with other functions/ business divisions.
  • Lead a team performing complex tasks, using well developed professional knowledge and skills to deliver on work that impacts the whole business function. Set objectives and coach employees in pursuit of those objectives, appraisal of performance relative to objectives and determination of reward outcomes
  • If the position has leadership responsibilities, People Leaders are expected to demonstrate a clear set of leadership behaviours to create an environment for colleagues to thrive and deliver to a consistently excellent standard. The four LEAD behaviours are: L – Listen and be authentic, E – Energise and inspire, A – Align across the enterprise, D – Develop others.
  • OR for an individual contributor, they will lead collaborative assignments and guide team members through structured assignments, identify the need for the inclusion of other areas of specialisation to complete assignments. They will identify new directions for assignments and/ or projects, identifying a combination of cross functional methodologies or practices to meet required outcomes.
  • Consult on complex issues; providing advice to People Leaders to support the resolution of escalated issues.
  • Identify ways to mitigate risk and developing new policies/procedures in support of the control and governance agenda.
  • Take ownership for managing risk and strengthening controls in relation to the work done.
  • Perform work that is closely related to that of other areas, which requires understanding of how areas coordinate and contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the organisation sub-function.
  • Collaborate with other areas of work, for business aligned support areas to keep up to speed with business activity and the business strategy.
  • Engage in complex analysis of data from multiple sources of information, internal and external sources such as procedures and practises (in other areas, teams, companies, etc).to solve problems creatively and effectively.
  • Communicate complex information. 'Complex' information could include sensitive information or information that is difficult to communicate because of its content or its audience.
  • Influence or convince stakeholders to achieve outcomes.

All colleagues will be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Values of Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence and Stewardship – our moral compass, helping us do what we believe is right. They will also be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Mindset – to Empower, Challenge and Drive – the operating manual for how we behave.

Embark on a transformative career journey as a Technical Product Owner at Barclays, where you will own Jira backlogs, user stories and sprint priorities while contributing to product roadmaps and delivery plans. You will translate complex business needs into clear requirements and prioritised backlog items, balancing value, dependencies, delivery capacity and risk within Agile teams.


Working across a complex data and technology environment, you will partner with business stakeholders, engineers, architects, analysts and data governance teams to deliver data products, platform modernisation and migration outcomes. You will combine strong product ownership with an understanding of data platforms, cloud and analytics, ensuring delivery decisions reflect business needs, technical constraints and governance requirements.


To be successful as a Technical Product Owner, you should have experience with:


  • Hands-on experience owning and prioritising Jira backlogs, user stories and sprint priorities, based on business value, dependencies and team capacity.
  • Experience contributing to product roadmaps and delivery plans within Agile delivery teams.
  • Proven ability to translate business problems, data consumption needs and change impacts into clear requirements, features and actionable backlog items.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across business, engineering, architecture, analysis and data governance teams.
  • Working knowledge of data platforms, data products, cloud and analytics environments, including data product implementation and consumption models.
  • Experience delivering data-centric transformation, platform modernisation or migration initiatives, including the prioritisation of data onboarding, data hydration and platform migration activities.
  • Experience supporting the migration of workloads from legacy platforms such as Teradata, Hadoop, Oracle or SAS to cloud-based environments.
  • Proven ability to identify and manage technical, data and business dependencies across multiple teams and workstreams, balancing business priorities, architecture constraints and delivery risk.
  • Understanding of data governance, data quality, security, privacy, regulatory and control requirements within delivery programmes.
  • Experience defining and measuring business outcomes, product adoption and benefits realisation for data and technology products.

Some other highly valued skills may include:


  • Experience working across multiple delivery teams, domains or stakeholder groups in a complex or matrixed organisation.
  • Experience managing competing priorities and shared or partial ownership boundaries.
  • Exposure to regulated, risk-led or control-heavy environments, including engagement with governance or assurance forums.
  • Awareness of how delivery decisions interact with risk, compliance and controls.

You may be assessed on the critical skills relevant for success in the role, including risk and controls, change and transformation, business acumen, strategic thinking, digital and technology, as well as role-specific technical skills.


This role can be based in Knutsford or Northampton, with a hybrid working model that requires a minimum of 3 days per week in the office.

title: Resiliency Analyst
description:
Position Title

Resiliency Analyst

Broadmoor Campus

Position Summary / Career Interest:

The primary role of the Resiliency Analyst is to ensure, protect, and support continuous business operations for the health system during times of supply chain disruptions- including medical/surgical, medical device and pharmaceutical. The Resiliency Analyst is responsible for carrying out the necessary research and analysis in detail to support all health system stakeholders, including building and maintaining a substitution product framework for all supplies and collaborating with other teams to build diversification of suppliers for like products meeting same fit, form, and function to promote risk mitigation for the organization. Monitoring trusted sites for weather and current events will be a key strategy for this position with the flexibility to adapt to new situations as they arise. The Resiliency Analyst will lead and organize multiple workgroups and task forces to provide both continued sustainment of medical/surgical, medical device and pharmaceutical supply chain resiliency, but to manage through complex disruptions. This role will require team members to possess expertise in communication both written and verbal and be equally effective as an individual contributor and a team player.

Responsibilities and Essential Job Functions
  • Identifies and diversifies sourcing strategies for defined products listed in item master (medical surgical, medical device and pharmaceutical).
  • Maintains documented knowledge of global manufacturing capabilities and update and communicates team.
  • Ability to influence others using data and documented evidence.
  • Builds out strategic reserve opportunities internally and in partnership with system distribution partners, GPO.
  • Works with leadership to develop disaster management, contingency and resiliency plans based on data and analytics.
  • Participates in planning sessions with suppliers to develop forecasting processes.
  • Works closely with internal business partners as requested, proactively building mitigation strategies to manage disruptions, including Category Management to build/insert scripted language around country of origin, risk sharing, productions schedules, transparency between both parties.
  • Participates with other Spend Management teams and Pharmacy Supply Chain in supplier reviews supporting transparency.
  • Leads resiliency workgroups and task forces related to the continuous evolvement of the program and complex supply chain disruptions (control towers).
  • Works with leader and peers to develop continual audits of all strategies to identify potential risks and vulnerabilities to organizational operations.
  • Participates in ongoing continuous improvement exercises to test strategies.
  • Must be able to perform the professional, clinical and or technical competencies of the assigned unit or department.
  • These statements are intended to describe the essential functions of the job and are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities. Skills and duties may vary dependent upon your department or unit. Other duties may be assigned as required.

Required Education and Experience
  • Associates Degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Supply Chain Management or a related field of study from an accredited college or university.
  • 5 or more years of experience in one of the following areas of supply chain: (Supply Chain Management, Supply Chain Analytics, Supply Chain Inventory Management).
  • 3 or more years of demonstrated experience in working with large scale projects and initiatives.

Preferred Education and Experience
  • Bachelors Degree in Business Administration; Healthcare Administration, Supply Chain Management, or a related field of study from an accredited college or university.
  • 7 or more years of experience in demand planning and forecasting.
  • 7 or more years of experience in leading large-scale projects and leading initiatives and working with corporate level executives.

Knowledge Requirements
  • Self-motivated individual with strong presentation and facilitation skills.
  • Ability to connect the dots amongst conversations, research and processes.
  • Fascination with researching current affairs and their impact on supply chain, globally.
  • Possess strong communication skills via written, verbal and audio.
  • Ability to navigate through calm and urgent situations with confidence and execution.
  • Ability to make decisions for the betterment of our patients and organizations.
  • Knowledge of how supply chain processes work from end-to-end.

Full time

R-57511

title: Food & Beverage Supervisor, Serrano Buffet
description:
Under the direction of the Assistant Manager, Food and Beverage, the Supervisor, Food and Beverage is responsible for the efficient scheduling and oversight of subordinate employees with the purpose of improving the quantity and quality of work done continuously and ensuring efficient and economical work operations. 4. Determines materials, equipment, and facilities needed for efficient operations. Ensures the cleanliness, organization & preparedness of the immediate workspace & adjacent areas. Ensures safety and security standards are in place and followed.

title: Director, Retail Media Measurement
description:
With a career at The Home Depot, you can be yourself and also be part of something bigger.

Position Purpose:


The responsibility of the Director, Retail Media Measurement is to develop and lead a center of excellence around retail media marketing effectiveness measurement. This person will define strategic priorities and build a roadmap to advance the retail media measurement framework, measurement products, measurement artifacts including weekly reports, monthly business reviews and quarterly business reviews. The role will oversee or directly manage measurement products like retail media cleanroom offerings and an advanced insights platform. This person will work closely with the sales organization to generate the proper reporting requirements, including custom reporting for top suppliers. This person is responsible for managing a team of analysts who work with the sales organization to develop insights and recommendations from campaign performance and client goals.


This is a highly collaborative, client-facing position. This person will collaborate with cross-functional teams, including sales, media planning, media operations, data science, monetization, audience, IT and product teams, to develop new measurement solutions and technologies that drive improved retail media performance and accountability. This person will be expected to work with clients on measurement needs, capabilities and may be required to explain measurement approach and models.


This position will oversee and manage a team who work with cross-functional stakeholders to deliver best-in-class solutions and define how measurement is used to support key decisions. This person will be accountable for end-to-end performance measurement, (creation of econometric/statistical/machine learning models, analysis of results, stakeholder feedback, etc.), participate in R&D projects and contribute to the innovation of new methods (Machine learning, ad hoc models). Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including media planning, data science, and product teams, to develop new measurement solutions and technologies that drive improved media performance and accountability.

Lead the mining, analysis, and interpretation of data to develop actionable insights for complex business challenges.
  • 10% - Cross Functional Collaboration - Partner closely with Data Science & Analytics, Retail Media+ & Monetization, Product, Technology, etc. to prioritize stakeholder requirements for dashboard / BI tools.
  • 25% - Customer Focus - Collaborate with sales and clients to understand their needs, diagnose gaps within current solutions, and generate buy-in on improvements that will drive meaningful stakeholder value.
  • 10% - Drives Results - Steer decisions around methodology to ensure that measurement solutions across the organization adhere to rigorous standards, driving consistency across functions.
  • 5% - Project Management - Lead updates to senior leadership on progress against key initiatives on the data & measurement roadmap.

  • Background in full-funnel marketing measurement, including direct experience building out media measurement frameworks. Experience covering retail and brand marketing measurement preferred

The Digital Products Configuration Management (DPCM), formerly known as Software Configuration Management (SWCM), department, is hiring a Senior Digital Product Configuration Management Engineer. The DPCM department provides innovative solutions through automation, continuous improvement, and a skilled workforce providing support for all digital products.


The term 'Digital Product' (DP) refers to, but is not limited to, the following software types and their associated data and documentation: embedded (tactical) software, applications, Built-in Test (BIT) software, reprogramming tools, simulation software, test equipment, configurable logic, Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) design, analytical tools used to formally qualify deliverable artifacts, Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) system models or related artifacts, Free Open Source Software (FOSS), and Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) software.


Note This position will be filled onsite at the RTX Facility El Segundo, CA.


What You Will Do


  • Perform builds and releases of digital products manually and/or certified pipelines
  • Facilitate the Digital Change Review Boards (DCRBs)
  • Maintain, control, and administer of the Digital Products Development Library (DDL) (formerly known as Software Digital Library (SDL) tools
  • Maintain control, traceability, consistency, and security of all configuration items across the digital development lifecycle
  • Perform and maintain configuration planning & identification, change management & version control, status accounting, and configuration audits
  • Manage digital product development/media libraries
  • Document and maintain guidelines and standards for dependency management, build and versioning
  • Provide DPCM Tool administration / management control/access to CM relevant tools/applications (i.e. Microsoft Azure DevOps Server (ADS), Git, Gitlab, Github, Jira, BitBucket, Confluence, ClearQuest, Subversion)
  • Administer/manage/use DevSecOps tools like Coverity, Artifactory, Jenkins, Nexus, GitLab CI/CD, Bamboo
  • Coordination of data transfers, courier support among various environments
  • Lead coordination of various digital product releases and interface with functional and program leadership ensuring on-time delivery and configuration management execution in digital development environment/areas

Qualifications You Must Have


  • Typically requires BS/BA Degree in Science, Technology Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) a minimum 5 years of prior engineering experience
  • Experience with version control and change management/agile planning tools
  • DPCM/DevSecOps technology, Information Technology (IT), and/or development/scripting experience
  • Experience with Automation shell scripting in Linux, Unix, and Windows
  • Active and Current Secret security clearance is required Day 1. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance

Qualifications We Prefer


  • Basic knowledge in Digital Product / Software Configuration Management principles, process, and implementation/execution
  • Experience with DP/SW CM tools (Microsoft Azure DevOps Server (ADS) - Git, Bitbucket, Jenkins, ClearQuest, Subversion, and/or Artifactory

title: Floating Universal Banker - Summerville, SC

The SouthState story is one of steady growth, deep community roots, and an unwavering commitment to helping our customers move forward. description:
Bring more to life.


At Danaher, our work saves lives. And each of us plays a part. Fueled by our culture of continuous improvement, we turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.

At Danaher, the Red Teaming Global Lead drives adversary emulation, red/purple team operations, and offensive validation. Enterprise security strategy and risk priorities are set by leadership; the Global Lead shapes and refines the offensive-validation strategy, then owns executing it safely — campaign planning, rules of engagement, legal/safety governance, reporting, and remediation validation. The Global Lead works independently and partners with detection-engineering, threat-intel, IAM, cloud, and app teams that each own their own environment.

  • Engineer/develop offensive capability: tradecraft, tooling, C2 setup, and automation for repeatable, safe operations.

  • Design the sustainability & governance model: safe-operations standards, legal/safety coordination, evidence handling, and remediation-validation cadence.

The essential requirements of the job include:

  • Extensive (7-9 years preferably) offensive security or red team experience, including leading engagements.
  • Experience planning and executing adversary emulation and red/purple team operations mapped to a framework such as MITRE ATT&CK, including rules of engagement and safe operations.
  • Hands-on exploitation and attack-path experience across Windows/Active Directory, identity, cloud, and application environments using command-and-control and offensive tooling (such as Cobalt Strike, Mythic, BloodHound, or Burp Suite).
  • Experience translating offensive findings into prioritized control and detection improvements with detection-engineering and stakeholder teams.
  • Experience coordinating global engagements across legal and works-council contexts.

It would be a plus if you also possess previous experience in:

  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field.
  • Cloud, OT, or AI red teaming experience.
  • OSCP, CRTO, OSEP, OSCE3, GXPN, or equivalent offensive certification.

title: Vice President of Information Technology
description:
Position Description and Purpose:

Founded in 1923 and headquartered in Grand Rapids, Michigan, Roskam Foods is a leading contract manufacturer that partners with world-renowned food brands, retailers, and food service providers to produce a myriad of frozen, refrigerated and shelf-stable products. We’re a scaled, diversified operation with over 2 million square feet of manufacturing and 50 production lines across 8 facilities in the U.S. and Canada. We believe in the power of purpose-driven leadership to generate value for all. And we’re on a mission to optimize the potential of our people and brands. We are passionate about multiplying possibilities for our employees and our partners.

Roskam Foods produces and packages food products with the goal of consistently meeting and exceeding customer expectations for quality, safety, and wholesomeness.

Key Essential Functions/Duties:

Enterprise Technology Strategy and Leadership

  • Develop and execute a pragmatic technology roadmap aligned with Roskam Foods’ growth, manufacturing, customer, and operational priorities.
  • Lead all IT functions, including enterprise applications, infrastructure, cybersecurity, service delivery, technical data architecture, integration, and vendor management.
  • Translate business needs into clear priorities, investment decisions, accountable owners, and measurable outcomes.
  • Support acquisition due diligence and integration planning, as applicable, by assessing technology platforms, cybersecurity, data, infrastructure, contracts, costs, risks, and required investments, and by helping execute practical post-close integration plans.
  • Operate as a hands-on executive who can move from strategy and governance into issue resolution, project detail, and implementation when needed.

ERP Program Leadership

  • Assume executive accountability for the Microsoft D365 Finance & Supply Chain program, including scope, governance, resources, schedule, risks, budget, quality, and adoption.
  • Complete and stabilize the Canadian ERP implementation, resolve open issues, and convert lessons learned into a stronger template for the U.S. rollout.
  • Kick off and lead the U.S. ERP implementation with disciplined process design, master data readiness, testing, training, cutover, and change management.
  • Plan and execute the incorporation of a recent Canadian acquisition onto the common D365 platform and standardized business processes.
  • Maintain a strong preference for standard functionality, limiting customization to compelling regulatory, customer, or business-critical requirements.

Manufacturing Systems and Business Partnership

  • Partner closely with operations, finance, supply chain, commercial, quality, and plant leadership to improve business processes through technology.
  • Ensure systems support the realities of complex, multi-site manufacturing, including planning, scheduling, inventory, traceability, quality, warehouse, maintenance, and production reporting.
  • Build credibility on the plant floor by understanding operational constraints, responding quickly, and balancing enterprise standards with practical execution.
  • Identify automation and digital opportunities that improve safety, quality, service, labor productivity, cost, and decision-making.
  • Partner with the business owners of Redzone, Workday, OneStream, and other functionally managed platforms to clarify responsibilities and provide appropriate IT support for architecture, integration, cybersecurity, technical data, vendor management, business continuity, and future technology decisions.

Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, and Service Delivery

  • Provide reliable, secure, and scalable infrastructure, networks, cloud services, end-user support, disaster recovery, and business continuity across all locations.
  • Establish a risk-based cybersecurity program with clear controls, monitoring, incident response, testing, awareness, and executive reporting.
  • Improve service management, issue escalation, root-cause resolution, asset lifecycle planning, and user satisfaction.
  • Protect production continuity and ensure critical manufacturing and business systems have appropriate resilience and recovery capabilities.

Data, Integration, and Digital Enablement

  • Own the technical data architecture, integration platforms, data models, system configuration, security, access controls, and reporting technology across the enterprise.
  • Partner closely with Finance leadership and the Director of Master Data. Finance leadership owns the master data governance function, including the Director of Master Data and support team; the Director establishes standards, stewardship practices, and data quality accountabilities.
  • Provide the systems, workflows, controls, monitoring, and technical expertise needed to enable effective master data governance and improve data readiness before each ERP phase.
  • Identify and selectively pursue practical AI opportunities after the necessary ERP, data, security, and process foundations are in place, prioritizing capabilities embedded in D365, Copilot, and Roskam Foods’ existing Microsoft investments that can produce measurable operational or financial value.
  • Advance the practical use of the Microsoft technology ecosystem—including D365, Microsoft 365, Teams, Power BI, Copilot, automation, and analytics—where there is a clear business case, appropriate governance, and an accountable adoption plan.

Governance, Vendors, and Investment Management

  • Establish clear governance and accountability across IT-owned and business-owned technology platforms, including decision rights, project prioritization, architecture and integration standards, cybersecurity, responsible AI principles, technology and vendor risk, business continuity, and investment discipline, in coordination with the appropriate business and functional leaders.
  • Own and maintain key IT internal controls, including system access, segregation of duties, system change management, cybersecurity, vendor risk, backup and recovery, and technology asset management; ensure controls are documented, tested, monitored, and remediated in partnership with Finance and other control owners.
  • Own the complete IT operating and capital budget, including annual planning, forecasting, cost control, technology investments, ERP program spending, and benefits realization.
  • Develop transparent business cases, evaluate total cost of ownership, prioritize investments rigorously, and identify practical, scalable solutions that maximize existing technology and produce measurable value within available resources.
  • Lead strategic vendor relationships, contracts, licensing, implementation partners, and service-level accountability.
  • Provide concise, fact-based reporting to the CEO and executive team, surfacing risks early with alternatives and recommendations.

Organization and Talent Leadership

  • Assess and develop the IT organization, clarify roles and accountabilities, and ensure the team has the capabilities required for the ERP journey and ongoing operations.
  • Build a culture of ownership, urgency, customer service, continuous improvement, and practical problem solving.
  • Establish and regularly report meaningful departmental metrics covering service levels, system availability, cybersecurity, project delivery, internal-control performance, budget performance, user satisfaction, and team capability.
  • Develop internal leaders while using external expertise selectively where it accelerates outcomes or fills specialized needs.
  • Create repeatable processes and succession depth so critical knowledge is not concentrated in a single person or vendor.

Operating Expectations and CEO Partnership

The Vice President of Information Technology is expected to independently lead day-to-day technology decisions and execution while maintaining close alignment with the CEO and executive team on enterprise priorities, material investments, risk, and major program decisions.

  • Bring forward technology strategy, ERP stage-gate decisions, material investments, and significant risk matters with clear recommendations.
  • Own execution after decisions are made and maintain transparent accountability for milestones, costs, risks, and benefits.
  • Escalate early when business decisions, resources, scope, or adoption threaten critical outcomes.
  • Communicate in business terms and avoid unnecessary technical complexity in executive discussions.

Operating principle: Think strategically, engage directly in the details, create clarity, and deliver measurable results without allowing material surprises.

Leadership Scope

title: Lead In Vivo Researcher – Yen - Lab - Therapeutic Genome Engineering
description:
Join a cutting-edge laboratory dedicated to translating next-generation genome editing strategies into transformative treatments for hemoglobinopathies and pediatric catastrophic diseases. As the Lead In Vivo Researcher, you will direct the in vivo aspects of our translational pipeline. You will be responsible for managing highly specialized humanized models, overseeing the precise delivery of genome editing therapeutics, and championing the highest ethical standards in animal welfare. This role requires technical mastery in stem cell biology and a deep commitment to the 3Rs (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) of ethical research.

Job Responsibilities:

Advanced In Vivo Research, Cellular Analysis & Therapeutics

  • Lead and execute complex in vivo studies utilizing specialized humanized and disease-relevant research models, including immunocompromised and hemoglobinopathy models, to evaluate therapeutic genome engineering outcomes.
  • Perform precise isolation, phenotypic characterization, and preparation of human Hematopoietic Stem Cells (HSCs) and targeted cell populations utilizing Magnetic-Activated Cell Sorting (MACS) and multi-color flow cytometry.
  • Execute the preparation, engraftment, and maintenance of advanced humanized research models to support translational studies.
  • Administer advanced in vivo delivery approaches for experimental therapies using minimally invasive techniques that support both scientific rigor and welfare-focused practices.
  • Conduct specialized procedures, including aseptic sample collection, precise dosing methodologies, and downstream molecular and flow cytometric analyses, as applicable to study design.

Animal Welfare & Ethical Leadership

Research Welfare & Ethical Leadership

  • Champion research welfare by proactively refining protocols to minimize stress, support environmental enrichment, and implement appropriate humane endpoints.
  • Collaborate with veterinary staff, Animal Resource Center (ARC) personnel, and research teams to ensure specialized research models receive high standards of care and oversight.
  • Ensure all procedures comply with institutional policies, applicable regulatory requirements, the ILAR Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals, and the USDA Animal Welfare Act, while incorporating the principles of Replacement, Reduction, and Refinement (3Rs).

Laboratory Leadership & Operations

  • Maintain meticulous and transparent documentation for all studies, including health monitoring, engraftment outcomes, flow cytometry data, and observational records.
  • Guide and mentor early-career team members on standard procedures, welfare-focused handling techniques, MACS/flow cytometry operation, and specialized HSC protocols.
  • Contribute to the development, optimization, and implementation of refined in vivo methodologies, minimally invasive treatment approaches, and downstream cellular assays.
  • Support the planning and procurement of specialized supplies, reagents, and antibodies required for humanized models and complex in vivo studies.
  • Maintain regular and predictable attendance to support continuity of critical ongoing studies and research activities.

Minimum Education and/or Training:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant scientific area is required.
  • Master’s degree or higher heavily preferred given the advanced scientific nature of HSC handling and genome engineering evaluations.


Minimum Experience:

  • 5+ years of research experience is required
  • 3+ years of experience is required with a Master’s degree
  • No prior experience required with a PHD
  • Strong knowledge and experience in understanding and application of underlying principles related to techniques being performed
  • Experience in R&D methods and processes in lab setting, and execution of research projects for the laboratory preferred
  • Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role
  • Crucial In Vivo Expertise: Demonstrated proficiency working with humanized research models, highly immunocompromised strains (e.g., NBSGW), and/or specialized disease models (e.g., Townes).
  • Crucial Analytical Expertise: Hands-on proficiency with multi-color flow cytometry and Magnetic-Activated Cell Sorting (MACS) for the isolation, characterization, and downstream analysis of hematopoietic and immune cell populations.
  • Prior experience with human Hematopoietic Stem Cell (HSC) handling, preparation, and precise in vivo delivery/transplantation is highly preferred.
  • Proven track record of supporting welfare-focused research practices, regulatory compliance, and protocol refinement to enhance care standards and minimize distress.
  • Experience working with specialized software systems and databases for meticulous record and data maintenance (including flow cytometry analysis software).
  • Proven performance and leadership in a comparable high-level research role.

Compensation

In recognition of certain U.S. state and municipal pay transparency laws, St. Jude is including a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This is an estimate offered in good faith and a specific salary offer takes into account factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. title: Senior Researcher/ Lead Researcher – Immuno-Oncology Preclinical Modeling
description:
Join our Team!

The Center of Excellence for Pediatric Immuno-Oncology (CEPIO) is seeking a Lead Researcher in the Center’s immuno-oncology (I-O) modeling core.


CEPIO is a cross-disciplinary center supporting the development and translation of innovative immuno-oncology approaches across St. Jude. The CEPIO I-O modeling core provides validated preclinical modeling expertise to support studies in cancer biology, immunotherapy, and therapeutic development.


The Lead Researcher supports the execution of preclinical immuno-oncology studies, independently performing animal procedures, therapeutic treatments, sample collection, and laboratory assays using established or modified protocols. The position translates experimental plans into organized, reproducible, and well-documented in vivo and laboratory workflows.


The ideal candidate will have strong hands-on experience with murine cancer models and preclinical therapeutic studies, including tumor implantation, treatment administration, murine monitoring, sample collection, and surgical procedures. The position works under the direction of the head of the CEPIO I-O modeling core to support efficient study execution and completion.


Job Responsibilities

  • Independently perform preclinical in vivo studies using established or modified experimental protocols.
  • Execute assigned study activities, including animal scheduling, treatments, procedures, sample collection, and study endpoints.
  • Perform murine procedures for preclinical cancer and immuno-oncology studies, including tumor implantation/inoculation, therapeutic administration by multiple routes (IV, PO, IP, subcutaneous), survival procedures, murine monitoring, and blood and tissue collection.
  • Perform wet-laboratory procedures supporting preclinical studies, including cell culture, tumor cell preparation, tissue processing, nucleic acid and protein preparation, PCR/genotyping, and molecular, cellular, and/or immune-related assays.
  • Implement established or modified protocols with limited guidance and troubleshoot experimental procedures as needed.
  • Monitor murine health and study progress; accurately document procedures, treatments, observations, samples, and study records; and organize and summarize experimental data and study results.
  • Maintain organized schedules and records for multiple concurrent studies.
  • Work with CEPIO laboratory and animal facility staff to support study execution.
  • Contribute to the development, optimization, and documentation of laboratory procedures and SOPs.
  • Maintain equipment, supplies, reagents, and study materials needed for assigned research activities; monitor inventory, assist with purchasing, and support routine equipment maintenance and calibration.
  • Provide technical guidance and training to less experienced team members in established procedures and laboratory practices.
  • Prepare and contribute to research reports, presentations, posters, and publications with guidance from the head of the CEPIO I-O modeling core.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
  • Regular and predictable attendance is an essential function of this position.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience in preclinical cancer research and in vivo therapeutic studies.
  • Strong hands-on experience with mouse models of cancer and/or immuno-oncology.
  • Experience performing rodent procedures, including tumor implantation/inoculation, therapeutic administration by multiple routes, survival/complex surgical procedures, animal monitoring, and blood/tissue collection.
  • Experience executing murine studies with multiple treatment groups, procedures, collection time points, and study endpoints.
  • Experience with cancer cell culture, tumor cell preparation, tissue processing, PCR/genotyping, molecular biology, protein or nucleic acid analysis, and/or cellular or immune assays.
  • Experience with genetically engineered mouse models, including breeding, genotyping, characterization, or experimental use, is highly desirable.
  • Experience with immuno-oncology therapeutic evaluation, biomarker analysis, or translational research is highly desirable.

Minimum Education and/or Training:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant scientific area is required


Lead Researcher Minimum Experience:

  • 5+ years of research experience is required
  • 3+ years of experience is required with a Master’s degree
  • No prior experience required with a PHD
  • Strong knowledge and experience in understanding and application of underlying principles related to techniques being performed
  • Experience in R&D methods and processes in lab setting, and execution of research projects for the laboratory preferred



Senior Researcher Minimum Experience:

  • Two (2) years of research experience is required.
  • No prior experience is required with a Master’s degree.
  • Working knowledge and understanding of underlying concepts and principles of experimental design.
  • Experience with the most widely used techniques used in the home laboratory.
  • Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role.



Professional Growth

The Lead Researcher will have opportunities to expand technical expertise in in vivo preclinical modeling, immuno-oncology research, laboratory methodologies, and emerging experimental technologies, while developing skills in advanced preclinical study execution and supporting CEPIO’s translational research activities.



We invite motivated researchers passionate about preclinical animal models and immuno-oncology to apply and join us in pushing the boundaries of immuno-oncology and immunotherapy in the fight against pediatric cancers.

Compensation

In recognition of certain U.S. state and municipal pay transparency laws, St. Jude is including a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This is an estimate offered in good faith and a specific salary offer takes into account factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the salary range and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current salary range is $60,320 - $105,040 per year for the role of Senior Researcher/ Lead Researcher – Immuno-Oncology Preclinical Modeling.

AAMCI-Management, Inc. in Maryville, TN is looking to hire a full-time Property Maintenance Technician to preserve the long-term value and desirability of our community. Can you manage your time well? Are you an energetic handyman who would like to take your career to the next level? If so, please read on!


This general handyman position earns a competitive wage of $21-$23/hour depending on experience.


WORK SCHEDULE

This full-time position typically works Monday - Friday from 8:00 am - 5:00 pm with participation in an on-call rotation required. (premium pay for on-call)


ABOUT AAMCI-MANAGEMENT, INC

Chartered in 1972, we are a residential property management company with the sole purpose of managing multifamily housing with a focus on low and moderate-income developments. We manage over 4,000 units in the Midwest and Southeast. In addition, we invest in multifamily housing and are involved in development utilizing the low-income housing tax credit program. Our driving force is to provide the best home possible for our residents to thrive.

We constantly aspire to deliver innovative and high-quality residential management with enthusiasm, integrity, and professionalism. Our employees are a critical part of that. We believe all of our staff should have the opportunity to grow and establish a career with us. Additionally, our firm offers generous benefits and competitive compensation.

As a Property Maintenance Technician, you ensure that our residents have safe, comfortable apartments in good repair and that they are happy with the level of service that they receive. You promptly address any concerns that arise in the apartments of current residents and make the appropriate handyman repairs. When a resident moves out, you work hard to make the apartment move-in ready for the next resident within 5 days of the vacancy. You are organized and keep accurate records regarding preventative maintenance, work orders, inspections, and inventories.

Always happy to help, you assist the manager with apartment inspections. You participate in our on-call emergency rotation for evenings, weekends, and holidays. You enjoy interacting with people and are known for being calm, friendly, responsive, and capable. With pride, you contribute to the cleanliness and curb appeal of the community. Each shift brings a combination of daily checklists and unexpected surprises. You love that you are never bored! And, most of all, you feel great about the important part you play in our success as a property management company and in creating a place that our residents are proud to call home!

  • 2+ years of maintenance experience
  • Basic understanding of plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general handyman work
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation


Are you mechanically inclined, reliable, self-motivated, and eager to learn? Could you work well as part of a property management team? Are you attentive to safety? If yes, you might just be perfect for this residential handyman position!

Fundraising Data Analyst is a diverse role. They are responsible for supporting the management of Face-to-face, Telemarketing and digital channels, together with F2F &TM and Digital fundraisers. The Fundraising Data Analyst takes the lead in managing and planning the budget & income for these channels as well as monitoring the results and predicting impact on set goals. The role also includes monitoring overall income from all channels, attrition and reporting on this. The Fundraising Data Analyst has a knack for data, is always looking to optimize strategies and find connections others might miss. They create and adapt reports, submit selections used for various campaigns and coordinate with partners and colleagues. The role combines supporting fundraising channel management, financial planning, data analysis, reporting, partner coordination, CRM management and providing design support.

  • Work closely with channel specialists to improve donor segmentation and to implement data-driven campaign improvements.
  • Support the development of a culture of data-driven decision-making across the fundraising team.

CRM Data Management

  • Act as the primary administrator and key user of the Engage CRM system, ensuring it effectively supports fundraising activities.

Examples are: HIPAA, Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act (EMTALA), Consent for Treatment, Patient Rights and Responsibilities, Important Message from Medicare (IMM), Medicare Outpatient Observation Notice (MOON), Notice of Privacy Practices, Medicare Secondary Payer Questionnaire (MSPQ), Advanced Beneficiary Notice (ABN). At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world.

Raytheon brings the strength of more than 100 years of experience and renowned engineering expertise to meet the needs of today’s mission and stay ahead of tomorrow’s threat. We deliver solutions that help our nation and allies defend freedoms and deter aggression, creating a safer, more secure world. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense.


This position is an onsite role in Tewksbury MA.


The Patriot Cybersecurity organization is seeking an experienced Product Owner to lead cybersecurity innovation and secure development across emerging software, hardware, and integrated capabilities in the Patriot system. This role serves as the tip of the spear for aligned cybersecurity modernization guiding advanced assessment activities, ethical hacking phases, vulnerability discovery, threat analysis, and recommending mitigation strategies to strengthen Patriot resilience against evolving cyber threats.


The PO will lead have a Scrum Master and Scrum Practitioners, drive Agile execution and deliver new cyber capabilities that directly support the cyber objectives. This individual will report to the Chief Product Owner (CPO) and the Cross‑Platform Team Lead (CPTL), influencing technical direction, security posture, development priorities, and product roadmaps for Patriot Cybersecurity.

This role operates with minimal oversight, manages moderately sized projects or processes, and is recognized as a subject‑matter expert contributing significantly to modernization strategy and the development of next‑generation cyber capabilities.

What You Will Do

  • Be a Product Owner for one of the Scrum Teams on Patriot Cyber.
  • Lead product vision, strategy, and backlog ownership for emerging Patriot cybersecurity capabilities spanning software, hardware, networks, and integrated system components.
  • Perform advanced penetration testing and ethical hacking activities, including scoping, threat modeling, attack surface analysis, exploitation attempts, impact analysis, and system hardening recommendations.
  • Apply structured frameworks such as the Ethical Hacking Phases and Cyber Kill Chain to identify weaknesses, assess adversary techniques, and guide secure design improvements.
  • Conduct vulnerability scanning and assessment activities and convert findings into prioritized risks, actionable remediation plans, and cybersecurity roadmap updates.
  • Drive application security analysis and secure development requirements for new Patriot software components and modernization initiatives.
  • Integrate outputs from scanning tools, penetration tests, CVA results, RMF changes, and exploitation research into Sprint planning and product decisions.
  • Develop, refine, and maintain cybersecurity architecture artifacts, requirements, strategies, design documents, and security policies supporting modernization efforts.
  • Guide creation and improvement of RMF/ATO documentation including SSP sections, POA&Ms, SAR inputs, PPSM entries, SBOM updates, HW/SW lists, and other CDRLs.
  • Partner closely with engineering, platform owners, and stakeholders to evaluate alternative solutions and ensure secure implementation of system enhancements.
  • Collaborate with leadership (CPO and CPTL) to align product priorities, resolve cross‑platform dependencies, and influence cybersecurity modernization strategy.
  • Work independently with minimal oversight to investigate complex, undefined cyber problems, gather technical data, perform analysis, and recommend system‑level improvements.
  • Communicate frequently with internal programs, external partners, and cross‑discipline stakeholders to guide secure development and influence policies and cybersecurity standards.

Qualifications You Must Have

  • Bachelor’s degree in a STEM field and 8+ years of relevant cybersecurity, engineering, or technical product leadership experience
  • Active and transferable U.S. government issued security clearance is required prior to start date. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance
  • Advanced expertise in cybersecurity fundamentals, compliance requirements, and RMF (NIST SP 800‑37).
  • Hands‑on experience performing vulnerability assessment, ethical hacking phases, kill‑chain analysis, and remediation recommendation.
  • Experience with NSA (FIPS), NIST (SP 800 series), DISA STIGs, and USCYBERCOM cybersecurity guidance.
